zh.CATEGORY: AI 协作 / 任务与 Agent 平台（Workspace DNA：Memory + Intelligence + Execution + Interface）
zh.ONE_LINER_2_LINE_SUBTITLE: 它不是任务工具，是一台「把业务流程一句话变成可运行 app」的机器：Projects 存数据、Agents 做判断、Automations 跑执行、Genesis App 当界面——官方把这套叫 Workspace DNA，把结果回流的机制叫 Living Loop。
zh.USER_SCALE: 官方 press 页只给三个累计量：150,000+ Genesis apps built、500K+ AI agents deployed、3M+ automation executions（未写统计截止日）。第三方评价：Capterra 4.7/5（67 条）、Product Hunt 4.7（108 条）、Trustpilot 4.6（745 条），2026-08/09 核对。可数的规模在 sitemap：17 个子 sitemap 合计 28,602 条 URL。MAU、付费用户、ARR 均未披露，本卡不编。
zh.STAGE_MATURITY: 成长期偏成熟，且刚完成一次平台化转身。公司 TASKCADE INC.，2017 年成立，旧金山，Y Combinator S19；2019-10 TechCrunch 报道 $5M 融资。产品线：2022-12 Taskade AI 上线 → 2024 Workspace DNA（Memory / Intelligence / Execution）成型、Automation v2 支持 durable execution → 2025 Genesis + Platform V6（Aurora 设计系统）→ 2026 平台化（API、MCP v2、100+ 集成、agent 发布），官方称 80 releases in 5 months。六个付费档，从 $0 到 $250。
zh.BUSINESS_MODEL_SHORT: 订阅 + credits 双轨。Free $0 永久（2 成员、3 个 Live app、1 个 agent、10 次自动化/月、250MB、1 个知识源，且无月度 credits，只能靠邀请/克隆赚）；Starter $6、Pro $10（月付 $20）、Business $25、Max $100、Enterprise $250（均为年付折算月价；年付对 Pro 及以上省 50%）。无学生/教育/非营利折扣（官方明确）。
zh.VERDICT_ONE_LINER: 它把「一个工作区」拆成四层同构（数据/智能/执行/界面），再用四种封装（项目/agent/自动化/app）把同一份对象图卖四遍；护城河不在模板数量，在「结果回流成记忆」这条环。
zh.VERDICT_BODY_2_3_LINES: 拔电测试判为原生：拿走 agents、automations 与 Genesis 一句话建站，剩下的是一张任务表加十种视图，价值掉一半——因为它卖的就是「不用写代码也有一个 app」。但要看清楚它的 AI 是什么：不是模型能力，是「任务到模型的路由」（TSK 阶梯）加上把业务流程塞进可控容器的工程能力。这也解释了它为什么敢同时卖模板、卖 agent、卖 app——它们本来就是同一份数据的不同壳。
zh.TLDR_1_HEADLINE: 四层同构：一份数据，四种封装
zh.TLDR_1_BODY: Memory（Projects 存数据）→ Intelligence（Agents 做判断）→ Execution（Automations 跨 100+ 集成执行）→ Interface（Genesis App 当界面）。四种入口指向同一个对象图：Projects 给人用、Agents 给问的人用、Automations 给系统用、Genesis App 给终端客户用。所以它既能卖模板，也能卖 agent，也能卖 app——不是三条产品线，是同一层的三种包装。
zh.TLDR_2_HEADLINE: Living Loop：结果必须回流成记忆
zh.TLDR_2_BODY: 官方原话：Memory 提供上下文 → Intelligence 做决定 → Execution 产出结果 → 结果回流成新的 Memory。最具体的一处设计是「agent 的记忆不是一个黑盒，而是一个 Project」——可浏览、可编辑、可搜索、可 fork。这一招把「AI 记忆」从不可控，变成工作区里一张能被人改的表；也决定它每用一次会比上一次更准。
zh.TLDR_3_HEADLINE: 28,602 页里，只有 14.3% 是手写的
zh.TLDR_3_BODY: sitemap 实测（2026-11-26，17 个子 sitemap）：程序化资源页 18,376 页 = 64.2%（templates 3,997 / generate 4,526 / agents 3,169 / automate 2,361 / prompts 2,205 / convert 2,118）；UGC app 页 6,135 页 = 21.4%（community apps + 495 个作者页）；手写营销内容只占 14.3%（blog 1,125 / marketing 867 / learn 435 / wiki 573 / docs 169 / compare 197 等）。197 条对比页再拆：155 条是 free-<竞品>-alternative，33 条是纯第三方模型对比（gpt-vs-claude 这类），只有 6 条是 taskade-vs-*。这不是品牌对比，是纯吃搜索量的结构。
zh.SNAPSHOT_ONE_TO_TWO_SENTENCE_DEFINITION: 产品定位：官方定义原文是 Taskade is an AI-native workspace. Taskade Genesis turns one prompt into a live, hosted app. Each app runs on Workspace DNA: Projects hold the data, AI agents add intelligence, and automations act across 100+ integrations。它在 SKILL.md 里写得更直白：The user is usually a business owner, not a developer。换成人话：给「有业务流程但没有工程师」的人，一句话生成一个能跑、能发布、能读写数据的 app。
zh.USER_PROMISE: 官方主张是「把业务流程变成 live app」。用户语言：你不用先学一套工具，也不用找人开发——把流程说出来，它给你一个带数据表、带 agent、带自动化、能挂自己域名的 app，然后你可以克隆别人的成品改一改。
zh.SEGMENT_1_NAME: 小团队 / 一人公司 / 代理机构（business owner, not developer）
zh.SEGMENT_1_DETAIL: 这是它自己写明的 ICP。他们要的不是「更好的项目管理」，是「客户门户 / CRM / 发票流程 / 预约 / 仪表盘」这类小系统，而买一套 SaaS 要钱、找人开发要时间。Free 档的 3 个 app 额度正好够试一个真实场景，Pro 的 10 个自定义域名正好够接客户。
zh.SEGMENT_2_DETAIL: App Kit 可以把「app 界面 + projects + agents + automations」打成一包，设成免费或付费，别人一键克隆，作者从 Earnings 提现；同一份 app 还可以出 free 与 Pro 两个条目。所以它同时是一个创作者分发平台——sitemap 里 495 个作者页就是证据。
zh.SEGMENT_3_NAME: 想搬家的团队（Notion / Asana / ClickUp / Trello / Monday 用户）
zh.SEGMENT_3_DETAIL: 它做了 30+ 个导入器（Notion、Asana、ClickUp、Trello、Monday、Zapier、Make、Obsidian、Evernote、Roam、Logseq、Workflowy、Miro…），导入即成为 project，可立刻挂 agent 与自动化。对比页里 155 条 free-<竞品>-alternative 正是给这批人搜的。
zh.JTBD_FUNCTIONAL: 把「一个业务的流程」变成「一个能跑的系统」：数据有地方存、判断有人做、重复动作自己跑、界面能给客户看。
zh.JTBD_EMOTIONAL: 不用承认自己请不起开发。它对用户的情绪承诺是「你也能做出一个软件」——这也是 Genesis 一句话生成最上瘾的地方：从想法到能点，中间没有排期。
zh.JTBD_SOCIAL: 在小团队里成为「把流程跑起来的人」；对客户，交付的不是一份文档，而是一个能登录、能提交、能看进度的门户。
zh.TRIGGER_MOMENT: 业务里同一个流程第三次靠人肉跑：客户问进度要手打、发票逾期要手催、入职清单要人盯。这时候人会去搜「有没有现成模板」，而它 3,997 个模板页 + 4,526 个生成器页就是为这个搜索准备的。
zh.FREQUENCY: 按业务流程频次走（工单/订单/客户跟进落在日到周的量级）；官方未披露使用频次，只披露累计执行量 3M+。
zh.USAGE_CONTEXT: 桌面/移动/浏览器扩展；数据在 Projects（10 种视图：List / Board / Table / Mind Map / Docs / Calendar / Gantt / Actionsheet / Org Chart 等）；判断在 Agents（指令 + 知识 + 持久记忆 + 工具 + slash 命令）；执行在 Automations（4 类触发 + 5 类动作 + 分支/循环/过滤/审批）；界面在 Genesis App（可发布到 *.taskade.app 或自有域名）；外部调用走 Hosted MCP 与 REST API。
zh.LOOP_TRIGGER_DETAIL: 触发点不是「我要用 AI」，是「这件事每周都要做一遍，而每次都是人在做」。它把触发做成四种：Taskade 内部事件（任务新增/完成/指派/字段变更）、外部 app 事件（Gmail / Slack / GitHub / Notion…）、时间（Schedule）、入站（Webhook / Mailhook / Form）。
zh.LOOP_ACTION_TITLE: 要么让 agent 做，要么让自动化跑
zh.LOOP_ACTION_DETAIL: 同一个流程有两条入口：人问 agent（它带知识、带记忆、带工具，工具可设「自动执行」或「需人工批准」）；或者系统跑 automation（触发 → 动作，中间可插分支、循环、过滤、延时、审批）。两条入口共享同一份数据，所以「先手动跑通，再让它自动跑」是这个产品最自然的学习路径。
zh.LOOP_REWARD_TITLE: 产物落回项目里，而不是落在聊天窗口
zh.LOOP_REWARD_DETAIL: agent 的产出可以写回 Projects（建任务、改字段、加评论），automation 的产出可以是新记录、通知、邮件、报告；Genesis App 则是把这些能力包成一个界面给终端用户。产出留在数据层，是 Living Loop 能成立的前提。
zh.LOOP_RETURN_TITLE: 记忆变厚，下一次判断更准
zh.LOOP_RETURN_DETAIL: 回来的理由不是「再生成一次」，是「它记得上次是怎么处理的」。持久记忆存成 Project，可浏览可编辑可 fork；知识源可以挂文件、项目、网页、YouTube、云盘（付费档 50 个/agent）。用得越久，越不像一个通用助手。
zh.LOOP_FREQ: 按流程频次走，日到周量级（[推断] 依据：自动化动作以「新订单/新工单/每日提醒」为主，官方未披露频次；只披露累计 3M+ automation executions）。
zh.LOOP_FREQ_NOTE_TRIGGER_CONTEXT: 同一个触发反复出现：又有一件事得按流程走一遍。它把这个动作从「人记得去做」改成「事件到了就有人做」，而审批步的设计说明它知道：不是所有事都能全自动。
zh.LOOP_ONE_LINE_INSIGHT_WHAT_THE_LOOP_ACTU: 它真正教用户的是「流程本身就是产品」：当你把一次处理写成一条 flow，你就有了一个可以交给别人、交给 agent、交给客户的资产。
zh.ACQUISITION_LOOP_DETAIL: 流量曝光：三合一结构，全部可数。① 程序化 SEO：28,602 条 URL 里 64.2% 是 templates / agents / automate / prompts / convert / generate 这类「搜什么有什么」的资源页；② UGC 克隆工厂：6,135 个社区 app 页 + 495 个作者页进 sitemap，且每个用户发布的 app 自动带 robots.txt / sitemap.xml / llms.txt——客户的产出变成新的发现节点；③ AI 原生发现层（GEO）：llms.txt（2026-11-18 更新，含 TL;DR、事实、FAQ、How to Cite Taskade 的指定引用措辞）、SKILL.md（给 agent 的操作手册）、Hosted MCP（OAuth 2.0 + PKCE）、.well-known 元数据（api-catalog、mcp.json、server-card、agent-skills 索引）、Accept: text/markdown、OpenAPI JSON、TSK-Bench，以及 robots.txt 里写明 ai-train=yes, search=yes, ai-input=yes。
zh.AHA_MOMENT_DETAIL: 官方叙事里最像 aha 的一刻：一句话 → 一个有数据表、有 agent、有自动化、能发布的 app，从想法到能点中间没有排期。本期未实测，这一点只据官方 llms.txt 与 About 页描述，不作体验结论。
zh.VIRALITY_DETAIL_OR_NONE: 有，而且做了三层：克隆即用（Free 可克隆 1,000+ free app kits，每次克隆占 Free 的 3 个 app 额度）、克隆给 credits（Earn Credits When Others Clone）、已发布 app 自带发现层（robots/sitemap/llms.txt）与公共 agent 页 + 5 种 widget 嵌入。「用额度做货币、用克隆做传播、用成品做商品」——这条闭环比单纯免费档更狠 [推断]。
zh.RETENTION_1: 数据 + 记忆都在工作区里：Projects 存业务数据，agent 的持久记忆也存成 Project，搬走等于重建整个上下文。
zh.RETENTION_2: 自动化一旦跑起来就是流程的一部分：100+ 集成、webhook、审批步，替换等于重新接线并重新验证。
zh.RETENTION_3: 已发布 app 有终端用户（App Users / GenesisAuth）：客户在用的门户，是最硬的留存——你不是在换工具，是在换客户的入口。
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_1_DETAIL: Free 档没有月度 credits，只能靠邀请（Earn AI Credits by Inviting Friends）与被克隆（Earn Credits When Others Clone）赚。于是「拉人」与「被复制」成了用户获得额度的唯一方式——这是把增长动作直接写进计费规则，比「邀请得积分」更硬。
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_2_NAME: 程序化 SEO + GEO 环
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_2_DETAIL: 模板/agent/配方/提示词/生成器五套程序化页承接各种长尾搜索 → 落地页给 Free 档 → 用户克隆成品后自己发布 app → 新 app 自动带 robots/sitemap/llms.txt，成为新的发现节点。前两条是它写的，第三条是用户替它写的。
zh.SURFACE_1_ROLE: 结构化数据：任务树 + 自定义字段 + 10 种视图（List / Board / Table / Mind Map / Docs / Calendar / Gantt / Actionsheet / Org Chart 等）。注意 2026 版站点里「笔记 / 思维导图」已经不是独立对象，而是 project 的两种视图——这是理解它架构的关键。
zh.SURFACE_2_ROLE: 一个有角色的 AI 队友：指令 + 知识（文件/项目/网页/YouTube/云盘）+ 持久记忆 + 工具（研究/文档/AI 步骤/工作区操作/外部 app/自定义）+ slash 命令。工具可各自设「自动执行」或「需人工批准」；多 agent 可组 AI Teams（Auto / Everyone / Manual / Orchestrate 四种模式）。
zh.SURFACE_3_ROLE: 触发器 + 动作 + 控制流（Branch / Loop / Filter / Delay / Approval）+ 173 个连接器（6 类）。触发有四类：Taskade 内部事件、外部 app 事件、时间、入站（Webhook / Mailhook / Form）；动作可返回结构化 JSON 供后续步骤取字段。
zh.SURFACE_4_ROLE: 一句话生成的 React app，由 Taskade 托管，读写上面三层；可发布到 *.taskade.app 或自有域名（含 SSL）、可 iframe 嵌入、可密码保护，并自带 App Users / GenesisAuth（独立于 Taskade 账号的终端用户登录）。这一层是它区别于所有「模板 + agent」产品的关键。
zh.SURFACE_5_ROLE: 6,135 个社区 app 页 + 72 个分类（48 类型 + 12 团队 + 12 行业）+ 495 个作者页；App Kit 可克隆、可免费/付费分发、可导出 .tsk、可导出 GitHub。它把「成品」变成了可流通资产——这是模板生意的下一层。
zh.SURFACE_6_ROLE: 给 AI 用的门面：Hosted MCP（https://www.taskade.com/mcp，OAuth 2.0 + PKCE）让外部 agent 读写工作区，SKILL.md 教它怎么用，llms.txt 连「该怎么引用我」都写好了。大多数产品把 AI 当用户，它把 AI 也当客户。
zh.ENTITY_1: Workspace（顶层隔离单元：每个 workspace 有自己的 memory / intelligence / execution）
zh.ENTITY_3: View（同一份数据的 10 种看法）
zh.ENTITY_4: Agent（指令 + 知识 + 持久记忆 + 工具）
zh.ENTITY_5: Automation / App Kit（流程与可流通的成品）
zh.IA_LOGIC_PARAGRAPH: 主轴是「项目」：一切从 Projects 进来，向上长成 Agent 的知识与记忆，向外长成 Automation 的触发与动作，最后被 Genesis App 包成界面。好处是四种封装共享同一份数据——改一处，四种入口都变；代价是概念密度极高：一个用户要同时理解 project、view、field、agent、tool、knowledge、memory、trigger、action、app kit 十个对象，才能完整发挥它。这也是它和 Notion 一类的分野：Notion 只要求你理解 block。
zh.NAV_INTERACTION_PARAGRAPH: 导航按「做什么」切：Create（Genesis）/ Projects / Agents / Automate / Apps / Templates / Integrations / Pricing / Learn / Docs。值得注意的是 /use-cases 与 /solutions 在 2026 版站点是 404——场景全部由 /apps/categories 的 72 类 app kits 与 /learn/projects/for-* 人群页承载。本期未实测，交互结论只据站点结构与文档，不下体验判断。
zh.CRAFT_1_NAME: 把 AI 的记忆做成一个能编辑的 Project
zh.CRAFT_1_DETAIL: 这是全站最值得抄的一处：持久记忆不是藏在模型里，而是落成一个 Project，可浏览、可编辑、可搜索、可 fork。结果有三：用户能看见 agent「记住了什么」，能改错，能把记忆复制给另一个 agent；同时记忆顺带变成了产品里的数据资产。
zh.CRAFT_2_NAME: TSK 阶梯：按任务档位选模型，而不是按厂商型号
zh.CRAFT_2_DETAIL: TSK-Auto / Instant / Standard / Thinking / Reasoning 五档，用户选的是「这活有多难」，不是「用哪个模型」；Pro 起可 BYOK（OpenAI / Anthropic / Google，Business 再加 xAI / DeepSeek / Mistral / OpenRouter）。模型是耗材，产品是「任务到模型的路由」——这是 2026 年 AI 产品该有的抽象，因为模型半年换一代，而用户的心智不该跟着换。
zh.CRAFT_3_NAME: 三种封装：模板给结构、App Kit 给成品、MCP 给机器
zh.CRAFT_3_DETAIL: Template 是「改一改就能用」的结构（3,997 项目模板 / 3,169 agent / 2,361 自动化配方）；App Kit 是「拿走就能跑」的成品（6,135 个，可克隆可售卖可导出 .tsk / GitHub）；MCP + SKILL.md 是「让别的 agent 直接调用」的接口。同一份对象图，三种交付粒度，三种买家。
zh.CRAFT_4_NAME: 用额度当货币，把增长写进计费规则
zh.CRAFT_4_DETAIL: Free 档没有月度 credits，只能靠邀请与被克隆赚；克隆别人的 app 又会占用 Free 的 3 个 app 额度。于是「拉新」和「被复制」不再是运营活动，而是用户拿到额度的唯一路径。这是把增长动机直接焊进账本，比「邀请送积分」硬得多，也解释了它为什么敢把免费档做小。
zh.CRAFT_5_NAME: 让用户的产出自动带 SEO / GEO
zh.CRAFT_5_DETAIL: 官方 Publish 说明：每个已发布的 app 自动产出 robots.txt、sitemap.xml、llms.txt；Business+ 还带 SEO Health 评分与 app analytics。也就是说用户每发布一个 app，就替它多开一个搜索与 AI 发现节点——UGC 直接变成分发资产，这是它 21.4% 页面来自 UGC 的机制原因。
zh.CRAFT_PRINCIPLE: 它的所有工艺都指向一句话：把「一次性交付」变成「可流通的资产」。模板可复制、app 可克隆、记忆可 fork、每个产物自带发现层——资产能自己流通，产品就不需要靠投放获客。
zh.TTV_LABEL: 价值到达时间：本次未测（本期没有实测，不把「生成出第一个 app」当成价值到达，也不换算成分钟）
zh.TTV_NOTE_WHAT_HAPPENS_AT_AHA: 可核实的只有结构：注册 → 选模板或一句话建 app → app 自带 projects / agents / automations → 发布。官方未披露 onboarding 数据，本报告不给时间数字。
zh.COG_LABEL: 认知负荷：高（未实测；可核实的是用户要同时理解 project / view / field / agent / tool / knowledge / memory / trigger / action / app kit 十个对象）
zh.DELIGHT_1: App Kit 克隆即用：6,135 个社区 app，打开就能看到它的「DNA」（用了哪些 project / agent / automation）。
zh.DELIGHT_2: 一句话生成的 app 能直接挂自有域名（Pro 起 10 个），带 SSL、可 iframe 嵌入、可加终端用户登录。
zh.DELIGHT_3: 模型换代用户无感：TSK 阶梯只暴露「任务档位」，不暴露厂商型号（付费档还可 BYOK）。
zh.DELIGHT_LABEL: 惊喜点：成品可克隆、app 能上自有域名、模型换代无感
zh.TRUST_LABEL: 信任：第三方口碑不弱（Capterra 4.7/67、Product Hunt 4.7/108、Trustpilot 4.6/745，2026-08/09 核对）；企业侧有 SAML（Business+ 起）与 SCIM（Enterprise）。但两处不确定：6,135 个社区 app 的活跃度与质量分布未核验；「一句话生成的 app」在真实业务里能不能无人复核地跑，官方没有公开的失败率或回滚机制说明。
zh.STRUGGLE_1: 概念密度过高：要理解十个对象才能发挥全部能力，而它的对手（Notion）只要求理解 block。这是它做大众市场最大的摩擦，也是它必须靠模板与 App Kit 降低门槛的原因。
zh.STRUGGLE_2: credits 计价对「非 AI 用法」不友好：一个只想拿它当项目管理工具的团队，会觉得 credits 与 automation runs 的额度跟自己无关；而 Free 档没有月度 credits（只能靠邀请/克隆赚），新人第一次用 AI 就可能撞额度。
zh.STRUGGLE_3: 规模口径自己没对齐：官方同时存在 1,000+ free app kits、500+ community templates、sitemap 6,135 三个数；另外月付挂牌价除 Pro $20 外都未核验。对一个主打「透明」的 GEO 玩家，这是它最容易被挑的一处。
zh.STRUGGLE_LABEL: 摩擦：概念密度、credits 计价、规模口径不一致
zh.REVENUE_MODEL_NAME: 订阅 + credits 双轨（额度既是成本也是拉新货币）
zh.REVENUE_MODEL_DETAIL: Free $0（2 成员 / 3 app / 1 agent / 10 次自动化/月 / 250MB / 1 知识源 / 无月度 credits）；Starter $6（10K credits、350 runs、3 agent、5GB）；Pro $10 年付、$20 月付（50K credits、1,000 runs、无限 agent、10 个自定义域名、webhook、.tsk 与 GitHub 导出、BYOK）；Business $25（150K credits、10,000 runs、无限成员与域名、白标与 SEO、SAML）；Max $100（400K credits）；Enterprise $250（1.1M credits、SCIM）。年付对 Pro 及以上省 50%。
zh.MON_ENTRY_HEADLINE: 入口小得反常，钱收在 credits 与「能对外发布」上
zh.MON_ENTRY_DETAIL: Free 档只给 2 个成员、3 个 app、1 个 agent、10 次自动化——小到像刻意设的墙：刚好够跑通一个真实场景，不够跑第二个。付费的三次跳：额度与 webhook（Starter/Pro）→ 对外品牌与域名（Business 起无限域名 + 白标 + SEO）→ 企业身份（Enterprise 的 SAML + SCIM）。它卖的不是功能，是「你能对外交付多少」与「你能跑多少 AI」。
zh.FREE_PAID_DETAIL: 免费：2 成员、3 个 Live app、1 个自定义 agent、10 次自动化/月、250MB、1 个知识源、7 天版本历史、无自定义域名与 webhook、无月度 credits。付费：Starter $6 给 10K credits 与 Hosted MCP；Pro $10 给 50K credits、无限 agent、10 个域名、webhook、.tsk / GitHub 导出与 BYOK；Business $25 给 150K credits、无限成员与域名、白标与 SEO、SAML、TSK-Reasoning；Max $100 给 400K credits；Enterprise $250 给 1.1M credits 与 SCIM。
zh.UX_MON_HEADLINE: 体验与变现是对齐的，还是打架的？
zh.UX_MON_DETAIL_ARE_THEY_ALIGNED_OR_IN_TEN: 结构上高度对齐，且对齐得很聪明：免费档把「跑通一个场景」的成本降到零，付费墙则立在「你开始对外交付」这一刻——更多成员（客户要登录）、更多 app（一个客户一个门户）、自有域名与白标（要给别人看）、更多自动化（流程开始依赖它）。这条线切得比多数 SaaS 准，因为它对应的是「业务真的在用」而不是「用户想不想升级」。打架的地方只有一处：credits 与 automation runs 是两种货币，用户很难预估「我这个月会不会超」，而超额的后果比功能受限更焦虑。
zh.COMP_1_D1: 同一批人：想要一个「什么都能放」的工作区的小团队与创作者
zh.COMP_1_D2: block 模型（页面即数据），靠数据库视图扩展结构化能力
zh.COMP_1_D3: 模板生态 + 社区 + 口碑；Taskade 有 155 条 free-notion-alternative 页直接抢它的替代词
zh.COMP_1_D4: 本次未核验（Taskade 的对比页给了替代叙事，但两边价格未在本期核对）
zh.COMP_2_D1: 要把业务数据做成表与视图的团队（它更结构化，Taskade 更流程化）
zh.COMP_2_D2: 关系型 base + view + automation，数据模型更强、AI 更后置
zh.COMP_2_D3: 模板库 + 企业销售；Taskade 用 templates / automate 程序化页接它的搜索
zh.COMP_3_D1: 已经有工具、只需要把工具连起来的人（「自动化」这一段链路）
zh.COMP_3_D2: 触发-动作编排引擎，连接器数量是护城河；不持有数据层
zh.COMP_3_D3: 集成目录 + 长尾「X + Y integration」搜索；Taskade 的 automate（2,361 页）与 integrations（180 页）正对着打
zh.COMP_4_D1: 要「把数据做成一个能给客户用的界面」的人——这是 Genesis 最直接的对手
zh.COMP_4_D2: no-code app builder：界面能力强，但数据与自动化要外接（Airtable / Sheets / 数据库）
zh.COMP_4_D3: 创作者社区 + 模板 + 教程内容
zh.COMP_OWN_D1: AI 协作 / 任务与 Agent 平台（一句话建 app）
zh.COMP_OWN_D2: Project/Task/Field + 10 视图 + Agent（含持久记忆）+ Automation（173 集成）+ Genesis App，四层共享一份对象图
zh.COMP_OWN_D3: 程序化 SEO 28,602 页（64.2% 程序化 / 21.4% UGC / 14.3% 手写）+ llms.txt / SKILL.md / MCP 的 AI 原生发现层
zh.COMP_OWN_D4: 六档年付折算月价全公开（$0 / $6 / $10 / $25 / $100 / $250），credits 与 runs 额度写清；但除 Pro $20 外月付挂牌价未核验
zh.COMP_INTRO: 名单不靠猜，直接读它的对比页结构：197 条 compare 里，155 条是 free-<竞品>-alternative（free-notion-alternative、free-zapier-alternative 这类），33 条是纯第三方模型对比（gpt-vs-claude、qwen-vs-kimi、glm-vs-gpt 这类，与产品无关），只有 6 条是 taskade-vs-*。这说明两件事：一是它真正在抢的是「免费替代品」这个搜索意图，对手是 Notion / Asana / ClickUp / Trello / Monday / Zapier / Make 这一串；二是它连「模型之间谁强」这种流量都要。竞品价格本次全部未核验，不做价格对比。
zh.COMP_WHERE_OWN_WINS: 三处别人短期不好补：一是四层共享一份对象图（Notion 缺自动化深度、Zapier 缺数据层、Bubble 缺数据与自动化的一体内置）；二是 App Kit 的可流通性（可克隆、可售卖、可导出 .tsk / GitHub，别人多是「模板」而不是「资产」）；三是 GEO 层的完整度（llms.txt 含引用指南 + SKILL.md + .well-known + MCP + Markdown 出口 + OpenAPI + TSK-Bench），这一套目前极少有产品做全。
zh.COMP_WHERE_RIVALS_CATCH: 三条缝：品牌与信任（Notion 是工作区的默认词，Taskade 还需要靠 155 条替代品页去截流）；数据模型的深度（Airtable 的关系型能力更强，复杂业务会被它挡住）；界面的自由度（Bubble / Softr 能做的界面，Genesis 还做不到）。还有一条更根本的：它把「一句话生成」当卖点，但真实业务 app 的难点在设计判断，不在生成速度。
zh.CHANNEL_1: 程序化 SEO 矩阵：28,602 条 URL，其中 18,376 条是 templates / agents / automate / prompts / convert / generate 六类资源页（64.2%）；另有 197 条对比页（155 条 free-竞品-alternative）纯吃「免费替代品」搜索。
zh.CHANNEL_2: UGC 克隆工厂：6,135 个社区 app 页 + 495 个作者页进 sitemap，克隆给 credits、售卖抽成、已发布 app 自动带发现层——用户的产出就是它的内容资产。
zh.CHANNEL_3: AI 原生发现层（GEO）：llms.txt（含 How to Cite Taskade）+ SKILL.md + Hosted MCP + .well-known 元数据 + Accept: text/markdown + OpenAPI + TSK-Bench，robots.txt 明确 ai-train=yes / search=yes / ai-input=yes。它把「被 AI 引用」当成一条正式渠道在做。
zh.FRICTION_1_TITLE: 概念密度：十个对象才能发挥全部能力
zh.FRICTION_1_BODY_WHY_IT_MATTERS: project、view、field、agent、tool、knowledge、memory、trigger、action、app kit——要同时理解这十个对象，才用得出它的四层同构。对手 Notion 只要求理解 block。这不是设计缺陷，是它把「平台」和「工具」压在一个产品里的必然结果；但它决定了新用户必须靠模板/App Kit 起步，否则第一次打开就是一个空工作区。
zh.FRICTION_2_BODY: credits（AI 构建与调用）与 automation runs 是两套额度，六个档位各给不同数值；Free 档还没有月度 credits，只能靠邀请/克隆赚。用户最怕的不是贵，是「不知道这个月会不会超」。对一个把透明度做成卖点的产品，这一处最该改。
zh.FRICTION_3_BODY: 官方同时存在 1,000+ free app kits、500+ community templates、sitemap 6,135 三个数字；累计量（150,000+ apps、500K+ agents、3M+ executions）也没写截止日。对外这是可信度问题，对内这是运营指标没统一的信号。
zh.FRICTION_4_TITLE: 页面规模很大，但手写内容只占 14.3%
zh.FRICTION_4_BODY: 28,602 页里，手写营销内容只有 14.3%（blog 1,125 / marketing 867 / learn 435 / wiki 573 / docs 169 / compare 197 等），其余是程序化页与 UGC。这意味着它的品牌叙事很薄：用户搜到它时常是「某个模板页」，而不是「一个观点」。对一个想从工具升级成平台的产品，这是长期风险。
zh.METRICS_INTRO: 官方只公开三个累计量（150,000+ Genesis apps built、500K+ AI agents deployed、3M+ automation executions）与 sitemap 规模。以下分两类：可核实的公开事实，与标注 [推断] 的「它应该看什么」——后者不是真实数据。
zh.NORTH_STAR_METRIC: 每周被真实业务使用（不是被创建）的 live app 数（[推断]）
zh.NORTH_STAR_WHY: [推断] 它的收入按 credits 与 app 数量分档，但价值只在「app 真的有人用」时成立。「已建 app 数」会被一句话生成灌水（官方那个 150,000+ 就是这类口径），所以真正的北美星必须是「周活跃的已发布 app」。
zh.INPUT_METRIC_1_NAME: 克隆 → 发布 → 有终端用户的转化漏斗
zh.INPUT_METRIC_1_WHY: 它的增长全押在「克隆即用」上（Free 可克隆 1,000+ free kits）。但克隆不等于使用：真正决定收入的是「克隆后有没有发布」与「发布后有没有 App User 登录」——这两个动作才叫「业务在用」。
zh.INPUT_METRIC_2_NAME: Automation 的周执行次数与失败率
zh.INPUT_METRIC_2_WHY: 自动化是它从「工具」变「流程」的分界线。执行次数决定黏性，失败率决定信任——一条每天跑失败一次的催款 flow，比没有这条 flow 更快让客户流失。
zh.INPUT_METRIC_3_NAME: App Kit 付费克隆的作者数与其收入分布
zh.INPUT_METRIC_3_WHY: 如果「创作者能靠 App Kit 赚钱」成立，它就从一个 SaaS 变成一个市场（marketplace 的网络效应比功能更强）。这条指标看的是创作者侧的收入集中度：只有少数人赚到钱，说明市场还没形成。
zh.GUARDRAIL_METRIC: AI credits 的实际成本覆盖率 + 免费档用户的 credits 消耗
zh.GUARDRAIL_WHY: Free 档没有月度 credits，但用户在 Free 上克隆、建 app、调 agent 时依然在消耗它的推理与托管成本。免费越受欢迎，成本越先爆——这条护栏不设，增长会先把毛利吃光。
zh.METRIC_BLINDSPOT: 没有公开的留存曲线、付费转化率，以及 6,135 个社区 app 的活跃分布 [推断]
zh.METRIC_BLINDSPOT_WHY: [推断] 程序化 SEO 的规模可以数（28,602），但流量不能从 sitemap 推出来——本期未取 Similarweb / Ahrefs 类数据。另一个盲区是 GEO 的效果：llms.txt 与 SKILL.md 有没有真的让 AI 推荐它，本身没有公开的度量方式，所以这一层目前只能算「做对了动作」，不能算「拿到了结果」。
zh.MOAT_REASONING_ONE_LINE: 四层同构 8、分发规模（28,602 页 + UGC）7、GEO 完整度 8、模板与 App Kit 资产 6、数据模型深度 5、品牌与信任 4，加权 6：能被复制的是模板与页面，难复制的是「结果回流成记忆」这条环与创作者侧的资产市场。
zh.HORIZONTAL_1: 从任务到 app：Genesis 把「管理一件事」升级成「交付一个系统」——同一份数据，多了一层界面。
zh.HORIZONTAL_2: 从自用到售卖：App Kit 让成品可克隆、可定价、可导出，把用户变成渠道（[推断] 这是它唯一能绕开「模板同质化」的方向）。
zh.VERTICAL_1: 72 类 app kits：48 类型（CRM、客户门户、仪表盘、发票、预约、追踪器、知识库、聊天机器人、落地页、店铺、表单、计算器…）+ 12 团队 + 12 行业。
zh.VERTICAL_2: 代理机构与客户交付（Business 档就叫 For agencies and client work）：一个客户一个 app，白标 + 自有域名 + 终端用户登录。
zh.PLATFORM_1: 开放接口齐全：Hosted MCP（OAuth 2.0 + PKCE）、REST v1 GA、Action v2 Beta、webhook / mailhook、OpenAPI JSON（v1/v2）、.well-known 元数据、GitHub 上的 mcp / skills / cli / awesome-vibe-coding。
zh.PLATFORM_2: [推断] 它的平台策略是「两端都做」：一边让别的 agent 通过 MCP 读写它（它当工具），一边把用户的 app 发布成独立站点（它当宿主）。这个双面位置比 Slack 的双向 MCP 更激进——因为它的 app 可以不挂在 taskade.com 域名下。
zh.OPP_1_HEADLINE: （我的判断）把「Living Loop」抄成记忆产品的默认结构
zh.OPP_1_DETAIL_WHAT_HOW_WHY: 怎么做：让 AI 的记忆落成用户可浏览、可编辑、可搜索、可 fork 的「一张表」，而不是藏在向量库里；每次任务的产出自动写回这张表。为什么：这是 Taskade 全套架构里最可迁移的一招，也是最容易被忽略的一招——大多数 AI 产品的记忆是黑盒，用户既看不见也改不了。
zh.OPP_2_HEADLINE: （我的判断）GEO 不是写文章，是把机器可读接口做全
zh.OPP_2_DETAIL: 怎么做：最低配三件套——llms.txt（写清事实、FAQ、以及「该怎么引用我」）+ SKILL.md（给 agent 的操作手册）+ 一个 MCP 入口；进阶再加 .well-known 元数据、Accept: text/markdown、OpenAPI。为什么：Taskade 证明这套能做成标准动作，而多数团队还停在「写一篇讲 AI 的博客」。
zh.OPP_3_HEADLINE: （我的判断）把「额度」当拉新货币，但要给非 AI 用户一条干净的路
zh.OPP_3_DETAIL: 怎么做：照抄「邀请/被克隆给 credits」这个机制（它确实把增长动机焊进了账本），但同时给「我只想用项目管理」的用户一档纯席位价。为什么：Taskade 的 Free 档小得反常（3 个 app、10 次自动化）是为了逼用户做增长动作，这对它有效，对只想管项目的团队却是劝退——两种用户不该用同一套计价。
zh.STRATEGIC_HEADLINE: 它的赌注：让「成品」变成可流通的资产，而不是让功能更强
zh.STRATEGIC_DETAIL_HIGH_IMPACT_BET: 三个动作叠在一起：把四层压成一份对象图（同一份数据四种封装），把成品做成可克隆可售卖可导出的 App Kit，再把机器入口做全（MCP + SKILL.md + llms.txt）让 AI 替它分发。前两个是产品动作，第三个是它的真赌注——在 AI 成为主要入口的年代，「被 AI 引用」可能比「被人搜到」更便宜。代价是它必须同时做三个市场的产品：协作工具、自动化平台、app builder，而每个市场都有一个更专注的对手。
zh.MOONSHOT_HEADLINE: 终局：不会写代码的人，交付的也是软件
zh.MOONSHOT_DETAIL_WHY_IT_COULD_RESHAPE_THE: 如果「一句话生成一个能跑的 app」真的稳定，那么小企业的软件采购会从「买 SaaS」变成「生成自己的 app」——那是一个比项目管理大得多的市场，而且天然带分发（每个 app 都是一个独立站点）。距离不在生成能力（这一层已经过剩），在两件事：一是生成的 app 能不能被信任到无人复核（失败率、回滚、审计），二是不同 app 之间的数据边界（客户门户里的数据，凭什么给另一家客户看）。它现在用 App Users 与 SAML/SCIM 在补第二件。
zh.RISK_INTRO: 风险按「可能性 × 影响」排序，严重度是我的判断，不是公司披露。
zh.RISK_1_NAME: 「一句话建 app」被上游模型与通用 agent 商品化
zh.RISK_1_MIT: 守住三件上游做不到的：真实数据的持久化与权限（App Users / SAML / SCIM）、可发布的托管与域名、可流通的资产（App Kit / .tsk）。把「生成」当入口，「托管 + 权限 + 分发」当生意。
zh.RISK_2_NAME: 三个市场同时作战，每个都有更专注的对手
zh.RISK_2_MIT: 明确只赢一条主线（建议是「代理机构交付客户 app」——Business 档已经这么写了），其余两线做成能力而不是卖点。
zh.RISK_3_NAME: 程序化 SEO 规模大，但品牌叙事薄
zh.RISK_3_MIT: 把 155 条 free-竞品-alternative 页的流量，导到一个有观点的品牌页上（为什么「成品」比「模板」值钱）。现在它 28,602 页里只有 14.3% 是手写内容，长期会被更会讲故事的对手截流。
zh.RISK_4_NAME: credits 成本与免费档消耗的错配
zh.RISK_4_MIT: 给免费档设一道真正的成本护栏（不是额度护栏）：限制并发的 agent 调用、把重任务排队、对 BYOK 用户降 credits 消耗。免费越受欢迎，这一条越关键。

zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_1: Taskade EVE（元 agent）：从一句话建 app / project / agent / automation，会列计划、问问题、跑工具、请求人工批准——它已经是一个「带审批的编排者」。
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_2: AI Teams：多 agent 同群，四种模式（Auto 路由 / Everyone 全问 / Manual 点名 / Orchestrate 规划）——这是「agent 组织」的最小形态。
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_3: [推断] App Kit + MCP 让 agent 能自己装配一个工作系统并交给人用，只差「谁批准它上线」这条链。
zh.AI_DISRUPTION_RISK: 两条：一是上游模型自己做成「一句话建 app」，它退化成托管与权限层；二是通用 agent（Claude / ChatGPT 这类）直接读表、建记录、跑流程，用户不再需要一个专门的界面。它现在的防守是把界面（Genesis）、身份（App Users）与分发（App Kit）三件抱住——因为这三件都不是模型能直接给的。
zh.AI_OPPORTUNITY_1: （我的判断）把「记忆可编辑」做成对外能力：让用户能审计、修正、复制 agent 的记忆，这是企业敢让 agent 碰真实业务的前提。
zh.AI_OPPORTUNITY_2: （我的判断）把 App Kit 做成真正的资产市场（作者页、版本、评价、订阅式收入），它就从 SaaS 变成平台——这也是它对 Notion 模板生态最不对称的一击。
zh.ASSUMPTIONS_ONE_PARAGRAPH_LIST_WHAT_IS_I: 可核实：官方 llms.txt 与 SKILL.md 原文（Workspace DNA、Living Loop、The user is usually a business owner, not a developer）、六档定价与功能矩阵（年付折算月价、credits 与 runs 数值、BYOK 与 SAML/SCIM 分布）、17 个子 sitemap 的页数（合计 28,602）与结构占比、197 条对比页的构成（155 / 33 / 6）、GEO 层的具体做法（llms.txt / SKILL.md / MCP / .well-known / Markdown 出口 / robots.txt 信号）、第三方评分（Capterra 4.7/67、PH 4.7/108、Trustpilot 4.6/745）、公司史与融资（2017 成立、YC S19、2019-10 TechCrunch $5M）。推断并已标注：频次、北美星与输入/护栏指标、竞品价格与协议细节（本次未核验）、App Kit 市场的实际活跃度。本期没有实测，所有体验类结论均不出。
zh.ASSUMPTION_1: [推断] 「28,602 页」证明的是页面规模，不是流量。程序化 SEO 的有效性取决于这些页有没有排名，而本期未取 Similarweb / Ahrefs 类数据，所以不能据此推断它的自然搜索表现。
zh.ASSUMPTION_2: [推断] 它的收入主力是 Business 与 Pro，而不是 Free/Starter：依据是 Business 档的定位写的就是 For agencies and client work（无限域名 + 白标 + SEO + 10,000 runs），而 Free 只有 3 个 app、10 次自动化，跑不了第二个客户。
zh.CATEGORY_POSITIONING_PARAGRAPH: 它站在三条货架的交口：协作与项目工具（Notion、Asana、ClickUp、Monday）、自动化平台（Zapier、Make）、以及 no-code app builder（Softr、Bubble、Glide）。位置上它在中间偏「系统」：比协作工具多执行与界面，比自动化平台多数据层，比 app builder 多内建的数据与 agent。这个「中间位」既是它的差异，也是它的解释成本。
zh.CURRENT_AI_USAGE_PARAGRAPH: AI 构建过程：它的 AI 不是「加了一个助手」，是把工作区按四层重写，再让 AI 长在每一层上。① 层（官方 Workspace DNA）：Memory = Projects 存数据；Intelligence = AI Agents 做判断；Execution = Automations 跨 100+ 集成执行；Interface = Genesis App 当界面。② 环（官方 Living Loop）：Memory 给上下文 → Intelligence 做决定 → Execution 出结果 → 结果回流成新的 Memory。③ 原子：Project/Task/Field、View、AI Agent、Agent Tool/Skill、Knowledge Source、Automation Trigger/Action、Genesis App、App Kit，共 8 个基元。④ 拼接公式：数据 × 智能（指令 + 知识 + 工具 + 记忆）× 执行 × 界面 = 一个 Living App。⑤ 智能层的抽象：TSK-Auto / Instant / Standard / Thinking / Reasoning 五档——用户选任务难度，不选模型厂商，模型换代用户无感。所以它和 Slack 正好互补：Slack 是协议层（让别人来接），Taskade 是模板层（把同一份数据封成四种壳卖四遍）。
zh.FINAL_BREAKS: 需要强协作与治理的大企业（成员上限、权限颗粒度、合规都不够）；只想管项目、不想要 AI 的团队（credits 计价是噪音）；要复杂数据关系的业务（关系型建模不如 Airtable）；要高度定制界面的产品（Genesis 的自由度不如 Bubble）。
zh.FINAL_MOAT_OR_LACK_THEREOF: 护城河是「中」：强在四层同构与分发规模（28,602 页 + 6,135 个 UGC app + 完整的 GEO 层），弱在每一层都能被更专注的对手单点击穿（数据模型不如 Airtable、自动化连接器不如 Zapier、界面不如 Bubble、品牌不如 Notion）。它真正的资产是那条 Living Loop 与创作者侧的资产市场——如果 App Kit 真能让人赚到钱，它就从「工具」变成「市场」，那是唯一别人抄不快的部分。
zh.FINAL_WINS: 四层共享一份对象图、把 agent 记忆做成可编辑的 Project、6,135 个可克隆的 App Kit、28,602 页的程序化 SEO + UGC + 一整套 GEO 接口（llms.txt / SKILL.md / MCP / .well-known）、以及「用额度当货币」的增长机制。
zh.SIX_INTRO: 六维是本系列的主框架：前三条看值不值，后三条看敢不敢用、会不会留下。
zh.AI_TYPE_REASON: 本片判为原生。拔电测试：拿走 agents、automations 与 Genesis，剩下的只有一张任务表与十种视图。
zh.SIX_1: 替掉的是「找人做一个小系统」这一段：原来要买一套 SaaS 或找开发（周级），现在一句话生成 + 模板改（分钟到小时级）。成本从「开发与采购」变成「订阅 + credits」（$0 起）。这是它最锋利的地方，也是它最容易被打断的地方——因为上游模型一旦直接产出 app，这段差价就没了。
zh.SIX_2: 它啃掉数据存储、视图、判断（agent）、执行（automation）与界面（Genesis）五件事；甩回的是「设计判断」：一句话能生成 app，但业务该怎么跑、字段该怎么设、谁能看什么，仍然要人定。它把工程的活接走了，把产品的活留下了。
zh.SIX_3: 能用，但要人改一轮：App Kit 是「改一改」的起点，不是终稿；生成的 app 在真实业务里通常要调字段、权限与流程。本期未实测，此判断只据官方文档与 App Kit 的配方结构（如 Invoice Generator Pro = 3 projects + 1 agent + 3 automations）。
zh.SIX_4: 兜底设计得比同类好：agent 工具可设「需人工批准」，自动化有 Approval step，EVE 会请求批准；但「一句话生成的 app」本身没有公开的失败率或回滚说明——这一层兜底仍是空白。
zh.SIX_5: 大体可逆：.tsk 导出、GitHub 导出、版本历史（Free 7 天 / Pro 1 年 / Business 5 年）都给了退路。不可逆的是「把客户拉进你的 app」：一旦客户在门户里提交了数据，换工具就等于迁客户。
zh.SIX_6: 个人换得掉（Notion 模板 + Zapier 能拼出七八成），团队换不掉：数据、agent 记忆、自动化接线、已发布 app 的终端用户，四样都在它这里。所以它的留存来自「资产在这里」，而不是「功能更好」。

en.CATEGORY: AI Collaboration / Tasks & Agents (Workspace DNA: memory + intelligence + execution + interface)
en.ONE_LINER_2_LINE_SUBTITLE: It isn't a task tool. It's a machine that turns one sentence of business process into a live app: Projects hold the data, Agents make the calls, Automations do the running, Genesis App is the interface. The company calls the stack Workspace DNA and the compounding loop Living Loop.
en.USER_SCALE: The press page gives exactly three cumulative figures: 150,000+ Genesis apps built, 500K+ AI agents deployed, 3M+ automation executions — with no cut-off date. Third-party ratings: Capterra 4.7/5 (67 reviews), Product Hunt 4.7 (108), Trustpilot 4.6 (745), checked 2026-08/09. The countable scale is in the sitemap: 17 sub-sitemaps totalling 28,602 URLs. MAU, paying users and ARR are not disclosed, so this card does not invent them.
en.STAGE_MATURITY: Growth leaning mature, having just completed a platform turn. TASKCADE INC., founded 2017 in San Francisco, Y Combinator S19; TechCrunch reported a $5M round on 2019-10. Product line: Taskade AI launched 2022-12 → Workspace DNA (Memory / Intelligence / Execution) took shape in 2024 with Automation v2 and durable execution → Genesis plus Platform V6 (Aurora design system) in 2025 → platform build-out in 2026 (API, MCP v2, 100+ integrations, agent publishing), which the company describes as '80 releases in 5 months'. Six paid tiers, from $0 to $250.
en.BUSINESS_MODEL_SHORT: Subscription plus credits. Free $0 forever (2 members, 3 live apps, 1 agent, 10 automation runs/month, 250MB, 1 knowledge source, and no monthly credits — they must be earned through invites or clones); Starter $6, Pro $10 (monthly $20), Business $25, Max $100, Enterprise $250 (all annual-equivalent monthly prices; annual saves 50% from Pro up). No student, education or nonprofit discount (explicitly stated).
en.VERDICT_ONE_LINER: It splits one workspace into four isomorphic layers (data / intelligence / execution / interface), then sells that single object graph four times over as four wrappers (projects / agents / automations / apps). The moat isn't the template count — it's the loop where results flow back as memory.
en.VERDICT_BODY_2_3_LINES: The unplug test says native: take away agents, automations and one-prompt Genesis and what remains is a task table with ten views — half the value, because what it sells is 'an app without writing code'. But be precise about what its AI actually is: not model capability, but routing from task to model (the TSK ladder) plus the engineering to fit business process into a controlled container. That also explains why it can sell templates, agents and apps at once — they were always the same data in different shells.
en.TLDR_1_HEADLINE: Four isomorphic layers: one dataset, four wrappers
en.TLDR_1_BODY: Memory (Projects hold data) → Intelligence (Agents make calls) → Execution (Automations run across 100+ integrations) → Interface (Genesis App). Four entry points, one object graph: Projects for people, Agents for whoever is asking, Automations for the system, Genesis App for the end customer. So templates, agents and apps are not three product lines — they are three packages of the same layer.
en.TLDR_2_HEADLINE: Living Loop: results have to flow back as memory
en.TLDR_2_BODY: Company wording: Memory supplies context → Intelligence decides → Execution produces results → results flow back as new Memory. The most concrete design decision: an agent's memory is not a black box, it is a Project — browsable, editable, searchable, forkable. That turns 'AI memory' from something uncontrollable into a table a human can correct, and it is why each run is better than the last.
en.TLDR_3_HEADLINE: Only 14.3% of its 28,602 pages are hand-written
en.TLDR_3_BODY: Sitemap measurements (2026-11-26, 17 sub-sitemaps): programmatic resource pages 18,376 = 64.2% (templates 3,997 / generate 4,526 / agents 3,169 / automate 2,361 / prompts 2,205 / convert 2,118); UGC app pages 6,135 = 21.4% (community apps plus 495 author pages); hand-written marketing content only 14.3% (blog 1,125 / marketing 867 / learn 435 / wiki 573 / docs 169 / compare 197 and so on). Inside the 197 comparison pages: 155 are free-<competitor>-alternative, 33 are pure third-party model comparisons (gpt-vs-claude and similar, unrelated to the product), and only 6 are taskade-vs-*. This isn't brand comparison; it is pure search-volume harvesting.
en.SNAPSHOT_ONE_TO_TWO_SENTENCE_DEFINITION: Product positioning: the official definition reads 'Taskade is an AI-native workspace. Taskade Genesis turns one prompt into a live, hosted app. Each app runs on Workspace DNA: Projects hold the data, AI agents add intelligence, and automations act across 100+ integrations.' Its SKILL.md is blunter: 'The user is usually a business owner, not a developer.' In plain terms: for people who have a business process and no engineer, one sentence produces a running, publishable app that reads and writes data.
en.USER_PROMISE: The official claim is 'turn business processes into live apps'. In user language: you don't learn a new tool and you don't hire a developer — describe the process, get an app with a data table, an agent and automations, on your own domain; then clone somebody else's finished app and adjust it.
en.SEGMENT_1_NAME: Small teams, one-person businesses, agencies (business owner, not developer)
en.SEGMENT_1_DETAIL: This is the ICP the company writes down itself. What they want isn't better project management, it's small systems — a client portal, a CRM, an invoice flow, booking, a dashboard — and buying SaaS costs money while hiring a developer costs time. The free plan's 3-app allowance is enough to try one real scenario, and Pro's 10 custom domains are enough to serve clients.
en.SEGMENT_2_DETAIL: An App Kit packs 'app interface + projects + agents + automations' into one bundle, marks it free or paid, lets others clone it in one click, and pays the author from Earnings; the same app can also exist as a free and a Pro entry. So it is a creator distribution platform at the same time — the 495 author pages in the sitemap are the evidence.
en.SEGMENT_3_NAME: Teams moving house (Notion / Asana / ClickUp / Trello / Monday users)
en.SEGMENT_3_DETAIL: It ships 30+ importers (Notion, Asana, ClickUp, Trello, Monday, Zapier, Make, Obsidian, Evernote, Roam, Logseq, Workflowy, Miro and more); an import becomes a project that can immediately take agents and automations. The 155 free-<competitor>-alternative pages exist precisely for these searchers.
en.JTBD_FUNCTIONAL: Turn one business process into one working system: data has a home, judgement has an owner, repetition runs itself, and the interface can face a customer.
en.JTBD_EMOTIONAL: Never admit you can't afford a developer. The emotional promise is 'you can build software too' — which is exactly why one-prompt Genesis is addictive: nothing stands between the idea and something clickable.
en.JTBD_SOCIAL: Be the person in a small team who gets the process running; to a client, deliver not a document but a portal they can log into, submit through and track.
en.TRIGGER_MOMENT: The same process is run by hand for the third time: a client asks for progress and you type it, an invoice goes overdue and you chase it, an onboarding checklist needs watching. That is when people search 'is there a template for this' — and its 3,997 template pages plus 4,526 generator pages exist for that search.
en.FREQUENCY: Follows the process cadence (tickets, orders and follow-ups sit at daily-to-weekly volume); frequency is not disclosed, only 3M+ cumulative executions.
en.USAGE_CONTEXT: Desktop, mobile and a browser extension; data lives in Projects (10 views: List / Board / Table / Mind Map / Docs / Calendar / Gantt / Actionsheet / Org Chart and so on); judgement lives in Agents (instructions + knowledge + persistent memory + tools + slash commands); execution in Automations (4 trigger types + 5 action types + branch / loop / filter / approval); interface in Genesis App (publishable to *.taskade.app or your own domain); external calls via Hosted MCP and the REST API.
en.LOOP_TRIGGER_TITLE: The repetitive job shows up again
en.LOOP_TRIGGER_DETAIL: The trigger isn't 'I want AI', it's 'this happens every week and a human does it every time'. It makes triggers four kinds: internal Taskade events (task added / completed / assigned / field changed), external app events (Gmail / Slack / GitHub / Notion…), time (Schedule), and inbound (Webhook / Mailhook / Form).
en.LOOP_ACTION_TITLE: Either let an agent do it, or let an automation run it
en.LOOP_ACTION_DETAIL: One process has two entrances: a person asks an agent (it carries knowledge, memory and tools, and each tool can be set to run automatically or require human approval), or the system runs an automation (trigger → action, with branch, loop, filter, delay and approval steps in between). Both share the same data, which makes 'run it by hand first, then let it run itself' the natural learning path of this product.
en.LOOP_REWARD_TITLE: Output lands back in the project, not in a chat window
en.LOOP_REWARD_DETAIL: An agent's output can write back into Projects (create tasks, change fields, add comments); an automation's output can be new records, notifications, email or reports; a Genesis App wraps these into an interface for end users. Keeping output in the data layer is the precondition for the Living Loop to work.
en.LOOP_RETURN_TITLE: Memory thickens, the next call gets better
en.LOOP_RETURN_DETAIL: You come back not to generate again but because it remembers how this was handled last time. Persistent memory is stored as a Project — browsable, editable, forkable; knowledge sources can be files, projects, web pages, YouTube or cloud drives (50 per agent on paid tiers). The longer you use it, the less it behaves like a generic assistant.
en.LOOP_FREQ: Follows process cadence, daily-to-weekly ([inferred] from automation actions being mostly 'new order / new ticket / daily reminder'; frequency is not disclosed, only 3M+ cumulative automation executions).
en.LOOP_FREQ_NOTE_TRIGGER_CONTEXT: The same trigger repeats: another thing has to go through the process. It converts that from 'a human remembers to do it' into 'the event arrives and someone does it' — and the existence of approval steps shows it knows not everything can be fully automatic.
en.LOOP_ONE_LINE_INSIGHT_WHAT_THE_LOOP_ACTU: What it teaches is that the process itself is the product: once you have written one handling into a flow, you own an asset you can hand to a colleague, an agent or a customer.
en.ACQUISITION_LOOP_DETAIL: Traffic and exposure: a three-part structure, all countable. (1) Programmatic SEO: 64.2% of its 28,602 URLs are 'search anything, find a page' resource pages across templates / agents / automate / prompts / convert / generate. (2) A UGC clone factory: 6,135 community app pages plus 495 author pages in the sitemap, and every app a user publishes automatically ships robots.txt, sitemap.xml and llms.txt — customer output becomes a new discovery node. (3) An AI-native discovery layer (GEO): llms.txt (updated 2026-11-18, with TL;DR, facts, FAQ and a 'How to Cite Taskade' instruction), SKILL.md (an operating manual for agents), Hosted MCP (OAuth 2.0 + PKCE), .well-known metadata (api-catalog, mcp.json, server-card, agent-skills index), Accept: text/markdown, OpenAPI JSON, TSK-Bench, and a robots.txt that states ai-train=yes, search=yes, ai-input=yes.
en.AHA_MOMENT_DETAIL: The most aha-shaped moment in the official narrative: one sentence becomes an app with a data table, an agent, automations and a publish button — nothing scheduled between the idea and something clickable. Not tested this round; this rests on the official llms.txt and About page, not on hands-on experience.
en.VIRALITY_DETAIL_OR_NONE: Yes, in three layers: clone-and-use (Free can clone 1,000+ free app kits, with each clone consuming one of the 3 free app slots), credits for being cloned ('Earn Credits When Others Clone'), and a built-in discovery layer on every published app (robots/sitemap/llms.txt) plus public agent pages with 5 widget embed options. 'Credits as currency, cloning as propagation, finished goods as merchandise' — a tighter loop than a plain free tier [inferred].
en.RETENTION_1: Data and memory both live in the workspace: Projects hold business data and agent memory is stored as a Project, so leaving means rebuilding the whole context.
en.RETENTION_2: Once automations run, they are part of the process: 100+ integrations, webhooks, approval steps — replacing it means rewiring and re-validating.
en.RETENTION_3: Published apps have end users (App Users / GenesisAuth): a portal your customers use is the hardest retention there is — you're not swapping a tool, you're swapping your customers' front door.
en.GROWTH_LOOP_1_DETAIL: The free plan has no monthly credits; they can only be earned by inviting people ('Earn AI Credits by Inviting Friends') or by being cloned ('Earn Credits When Others Clone'). So inviting and being copied become the only ways a user gets allowance — growth written directly into the billing rules, harder than 'earn points for referrals'.
en.GROWTH_LOOP_2_DETAIL: Five families of programmatic pages catch every long tail → landing pages feed the free tier → a user clones a finished app and publishes their own → the new app automatically ships robots/sitemap/llms.txt and becomes another discovery node. The first two are written by Taskade; the third is written by its users on its behalf.
en.SURFACE_1_ROLE: Structured data: a task tree plus custom fields plus 10 views (List / Board / Table / Mind Map / Docs / Calendar / Gantt / Actionsheet / Org Chart and more). Note that on the 2026 site 'notes' and 'mind map' are no longer separate objects but two views of a project — that detail is the key to reading its architecture.
en.SURFACE_2_ROLE: A role-shaped AI teammate: instructions + knowledge (files / projects / web / YouTube / cloud drives) + persistent memory + tools (research / documents / AI steps / workspace operations / external apps / custom) + slash commands. Each tool can run automatically or require human approval; multiple agents can form AI Teams (Auto / Everyone / Manual / Orchestrate).
en.SURFACE_3_ROLE: Triggers + actions + control flow (Branch / Loop / Filter / Delay / Approval) across 173 connectors in 6 categories. Four trigger types — internal Taskade events, external app events, time, and inbound (Webhook / Mailhook / Form); actions can return structured JSON for later steps to read fields from.
en.SURFACE_4_ROLE: A React app generated from one sentence, hosted by Taskade, reading and writing the three layers below; publishable to *.taskade.app or your own domain (with SSL), embeddable via iframe, password-protectable, and shipping App Users / GenesisAuth (an end-user login independent of Taskade accounts). This layer is what separates it from every 'templates + agent' product.
en.SURFACE_5_NAME: App Factory / App Kits (the distribution layer)
en.SURFACE_5_ROLE: 6,135 community app pages across 72 categories (48 types + 12 teams + 12 industries) plus 495 author pages; an App Kit can be cloned, distributed free or paid, exported as .tsk, or exported to GitHub. It turns 'finished goods' into a circulating asset — the next floor above the template business.
en.SURFACE_6_ROLE: A front door built for AI: Hosted MCP (https://www.taskade.com/mcp, OAuth 2.0 + PKCE) lets external agents read and write the workspace, SKILL.md teaches them how, and llms.txt even specifies how it wants to be cited. Most products treat AI as a user; this one treats AI as a customer too.
en.ENTITY_1: Workspace (the top isolation unit: each workspace gets its own memory, intelligence and execution)
en.ENTITY_3: View (10 ways of looking at the same data)
en.ENTITY_5: Automation / App Kit (the process and the circulating finished good)
en.IA_LOGIC_PARAGRAPH: The spine is the project: everything enters through Projects, grows upward into an Agent's knowledge and memory, outward into an Automation's triggers and actions, and is finally wrapped as an interface by Genesis App. The upside is that four wrappers share one dataset — change it once, all four entrances change. The cost is concept density: a user must hold ten objects at once (project, view, field, agent, tool, knowledge, memory, trigger, action, app kit) to get the whole product. That is the dividing line with Notion, which only asks you to understand blocks.
en.NAV_INTERACTION_PARAGRAPH: Navigation is cut by what you do: Create (Genesis) / Projects / Agents / Automate / Apps / Templates / Integrations / Pricing / Learn / Docs. Notably /use-cases and /solutions both 404 on the 2026 site — scenarios are carried entirely by the 72 app-kit categories at /apps/categories and the /learn/projects/for-* audience pages. Not tested this round; interaction claims rest on site structure and docs only, with no experience verdict.
en.CRAFT_1_NAME: Make the AI's memory an editable Project
en.CRAFT_1_DETAIL: The most copyable detail in the whole product: persistent memory is not hidden in the model, it lands as a Project that can be browsed, edited, searched and forked. Three consequences — users can see what the agent 'remembers', they can correct it, and they can copy that memory to another agent; meanwhile the memory doubles as a data asset inside the product.
en.CRAFT_2_NAME: The TSK ladder: pick a task level, not a vendor's model
en.CRAFT_2_DETAIL: Five levels — TSK-Auto / Instant / Standard / Thinking / Reasoning — where the user chooses how hard the job is, not which model to use; from Pro you can bring your own key (OpenAI / Anthropic / Google, plus xAI / DeepSeek / Mistral / OpenRouter on Business). Models are consumables; the product is the routing from task to model. That is the right abstraction for 2026, because models change every six months and the user's mental model shouldn't change with them.
en.CRAFT_3_NAME: Three wrappers: templates give structure, App Kits give finished goods, MCP gives machines
en.CRAFT_3_DETAIL: A Template is structure you adjust (3,997 project templates / 3,169 agents / 2,361 automation recipes); an App Kit is a finished good you take away (6,135 of them, cloneable, sellable, exportable as .tsk or to GitHub); MCP + SKILL.md is the interface that lets other agents call it. One object graph, three delivery granularities, three kinds of buyer.
en.CRAFT_4_NAME: Credits as currency: growth written into the billing rules
en.CRAFT_4_DETAIL: The free plan has no monthly credits — they only come from inviting people or being cloned; and cloning someone's app consumes one of the free plan's 3 app slots. So acquisition and being copied stop being marketing campaigns and become the only route to allowance. That welds the growth motive into the ledger, far harder than 'invite a friend for points', and explains why it dares to make the free tier so small.
en.CRAFT_5_NAME: Every user's output ships with SEO / GEO built in
en.CRAFT_5_DETAIL: Per the official publishing docs, every published app automatically produces robots.txt, sitemap.xml and llms.txt; Business+ adds an SEO Health score and app analytics. So every app a user publishes opens one more search and AI discovery node — UGC becomes distribution, which is the mechanism behind the 21.4% of pages that come from users.
en.CRAFT_PRINCIPLE: Every craft decision points at one sentence: turn one-off delivery into a circulating asset. Templates copy, apps clone, memory forks, and every artifact ships its own discovery layer. When the assets circulate by themselves, the product doesn't need paid acquisition.
en.TTV_LABEL: Time to value: not measured this round (no hands-on test; generating the first app is not counted as value, and no minutes are claimed)
en.TTV_NOTE_WHAT_HAPPENS_AT_AHA: Only the structure is verifiable: sign up → pick a template or build an app from one sentence → the app arrives with projects, agents and automations → publish. Onboarding data is not disclosed, so no time figure is given.
en.COG_LABEL: Cognitive load: high (not measured; the verifiable part is that a user must hold ten objects at once — project, view, field, agent, tool, knowledge, memory, trigger, action, app kit)
en.DELIGHT_1: Clone-and-use App Kits: 6,135 community apps, and you can see an app's 'DNA' (which projects, agents and automations it uses) before cloning.
en.DELIGHT_2: A one-sentence app can sit on your own domain (10 of them from Pro) with SSL, iframe embedding and end-user login.
en.DELIGHT_3: Model generations pass invisibly: the TSK ladder exposes task levels, not vendor model names (and paid tiers allow BYOK).
en.DELIGHT_LABEL: Delight: cloneable finished goods, apps on your own domain, model churn you never feel
en.TRUST_LABEL: Trust: third-party ratings are respectable (Capterra 4.7/67, Product Hunt 4.7/108, Trustpilot 4.6/745, checked 2026-08/09), and the enterprise side has SAML (Business+) and SCIM (Enterprise). Two uncertainties remain: the activity and quality distribution of those 6,135 community apps were not verified, and there is no public failure-rate or rollback documentation for 'one sentence generates an app' running unattended in a real business.
en.STRUGGLE_1: Concept density is too high: ten objects must be understood before the product gives everything, while its rival Notion asks only for blocks. That is its biggest friction with a mainstream audience, and the reason it has to lower the bar with templates and App Kits.
en.STRUGGLE_2: Credits pricing is hostile to non-AI use: a team that just wants a project tool finds credits and automation-run allowances irrelevant, while the free plan has no monthly credits at all (only invites and clones earn them), so a newcomer can hit the limit on their first AI use.
en.STRUGGLE_3: Its own scale numbers don't line up: 1,000+ free app kits, 500+ community templates and 6,135 sitemap entries coexist; and apart from Pro at $20 monthly, monthly list prices were not verified. For a player whose pitch includes transparency, this is the easiest place to attack.
en.STRUGGLE_LABEL: Friction: concept density, credits pricing, inconsistent scale figures
en.REVENUE_MODEL_NAME: Subscription plus credits (the allowance is both a cost and an acquisition currency)
en.REVENUE_MODEL_DETAIL: Free $0 (2 members / 3 apps / 1 agent / 10 automation runs per month / 250MB / 1 knowledge source / no monthly credits); Starter $6 (10K credits, 350 runs, 3 agents, 5GB); Pro $10 annual and $20 monthly (50K credits, 1,000 runs, unlimited agents, 10 custom domains, webhooks, .tsk and GitHub export, BYOK); Business $25 (150K credits, 10,000 runs, unlimited members and domains, white-label and SEO, SAML); Max $100 (400K credits); Enterprise $250 (1.1M credits, SCIM). Annual saves 50% from Pro up.
en.MON_ENTRY_HEADLINE: The entry is unusually small; the money is in credits and in being allowed to publish
en.MON_ENTRY_DETAIL: The free tier gives 2 members, 3 apps, 1 agent and 10 automation runs — small enough to look deliberately walled: exactly enough to get one real scenario running, not enough for a second. Three paid steps: allowance and webhooks (Starter/Pro) → external branding and domains (unlimited domains plus white-label and SEO from Business) → enterprise identity (SAML and SCIM on Enterprise). It doesn't sell features; it sells how much you can deliver outward and how much AI you can run.
en.FREE_PAID_DETAIL: Free: 2 members, 3 live apps, 1 custom agent, 10 automation runs per month, 250MB, 1 knowledge source, 7-day version history, no custom domains or webhooks, no monthly credits. Paid: Starter $6 brings 10K credits and Hosted MCP; Pro $10 brings 50K credits, unlimited agents, 10 domains, webhooks, .tsk / GitHub export and BYOK; Business $25 brings 150K credits, unlimited members and domains, white-label and SEO, SAML and TSK-Reasoning; Max $100 brings 400K credits; Enterprise $250 brings 1.1M credits and SCIM.
en.UX_MON_HEADLINE: Are experience and monetisation aligned, or fighting?
en.UX_MON_DETAIL_ARE_THEY_ALIGNED_OR_IN_TEN: Structurally very aligned, and cleverly so: the free tier drops the cost of 'get one scenario running' to zero, and the paywall stands exactly at the moment you start delivering outward — more members (clients need a login), more apps (one portal per client), your own domain and white-label (someone else will look at it), more automation (the process starts depending on it). That line is better drawn than most SaaS manages, because it tracks 'the business is really using it' rather than 'the user feels like upgrading'. The one place they fight: credits and automation runs are two currencies, users cannot forecast whether they will exceed either, and the consequence of overage is more anxiety-inducing than a feature limit.
en.COMP_1_D1: The same people: small teams and creators who want one workspace where everything fits
en.COMP_1_D2: The block model (a page is data), extended into structure by database views
en.COMP_1_D3: Template ecosystem, community and word of mouth; Taskade runs 155 free-notion-alternative pages aimed straight at its substitute searches
en.COMP_1_D4: Not verified this round (Taskade's comparison pages carry the substitute narrative; neither price list was checked)
en.COMP_2_D1: Teams that want business data as tables and views (more structured than Taskade, less process-shaped)
en.COMP_2_D2: Relational base plus views and automation — stronger data model, AI layered later
en.COMP_2_D3: Template gallery and enterprise sales; Taskade catches its searches with templates and automate pages
en.COMP_3_D1: People who already have tools and only need them connected (the automation link in the chain)
en.COMP_3_D2: A trigger-action orchestration engine; connector count is the moat, and it holds no data layer
en.COMP_3_D3: Integration directories plus long-tail 'X + Y integration' search; Taskade's automate (2,361 pages) and integrations (180 pages) point straight at it
en.COMP_4_D1: People who want 'turn data into an interface a client can use' — Genesis's most direct rivals
en.COMP_4_D2: No-code app builders: strong on interface, but data and automation come from outside (Airtable / Sheets / a database)
en.COMP_4_D3: Creator communities, template galleries and tutorial content
en.COMP_OWN_D1: AI collaboration / tasks and agents platform (one sentence builds an app)
en.COMP_OWN_D2: Project/Task/Field plus 10 views, Agents with persistent memory, Automations across 173 integrations, and Genesis App — all four sharing one object graph
en.COMP_OWN_D3: 28,602 programmatic pages (64.2% programmatic / 21.4% UGC / 14.3% hand-written) plus an AI-native discovery layer of llms.txt / SKILL.md / MCP
en.COMP_OWN_D4: All six annual-equivalent monthly prices are public ($0 / $6 / $10 / $25 / $100 / $250) with credits and run allowances spelled out; monthly list prices other than Pro's $20 were not verified
en.COMP_INTRO: The list isn't guesswork; read its comparison-page structure directly. Of 197 /compare/* pages, 155 are free-<competitor>-alternative (free-notion-alternative, free-zapier-alternative and similar), 33 are pure third-party model comparisons (gpt-vs-claude, qwen-vs-kimi, glm-vs-gpt — unrelated to the product), and only 6 are taskade-vs-*. That says two things: what it is really chasing is the 'free alternative' search intent, against Notion / Asana / ClickUp / Trello / Monday / Zapier / Make; and it will take even the 'which model is better' traffic. Competitor prices were not verified this round, so no price comparison is offered.
en.COMP_WHERE_OWN_WINS: Three things rivals can't close quickly: four layers sharing one object graph (Notion lacks automation depth, Zapier lacks a data layer, Bubble lacks built-in data and automation); the circulation of App Kits (cloneable, sellable, exportable as .tsk or to GitHub — others ship templates, not assets); and the completeness of the GEO layer (llms.txt with citation guidance + SKILL.md + .well-known + MCP + markdown output + OpenAPI + TSK-Bench), which almost nobody has assembled.
en.COMP_WHERE_RIVALS_CATCH: Three gaps: brand and trust (Notion owns the word 'workspace', Taskade still intercepts with 155 substitute pages); data-model depth (Airtable's relational strength blocks complex businesses); and interface freedom (Bubble and Softr can build interfaces Genesis cannot). One deeper issue: it sells 'one sentence generates' as the headline, but the hard part of a real business app is design judgement, not generation speed.
en.CHANNEL_1: A programmatic SEO matrix: 28,602 URLs, of which 18,376 are resource pages across templates / agents / automate / prompts / convert / generate (64.2%), plus 197 comparison pages (155 of them free-competitor-alternative) harvesting 'free alternative' searches.
en.CHANNEL_2: A UGC clone factory: 6,135 community app pages and 495 author pages in the sitemap, credits for being cloned, a revenue share on sales, and a discovery layer on every published app — user output is its content asset.
en.CHANNEL_3: An AI-native discovery layer (GEO): llms.txt (including 'How to Cite Taskade') + SKILL.md + Hosted MCP + .well-known metadata + Accept: text/markdown + OpenAPI + TSK-Bench, with robots.txt explicitly stating ai-train=yes / search=yes / ai-input=yes. It treats 'being cited by AI' as a formal channel.
en.FRICTION_1_TITLE: Concept density: ten objects before the product gives everything
en.FRICTION_1_BODY_WHY_IT_MATTERS: Project, view, field, agent, tool, knowledge, memory, trigger, action, app kit — all ten have to be understood to use the four-layer architecture. Notion only asks for blocks. This isn't a design defect; it is the inevitable result of compressing a platform and a tool into one product. But it means new users must start from a template or an App Kit, or their first screen is an empty workspace.
en.FRICTION_2_TITLE: Two currencies, no way to budget
en.FRICTION_2_BODY: Credits (AI building and calls) and automation runs are two separate allowances, each different across six tiers, and the free plan has no monthly credits at all. What users fear isn't cost, it's not knowing whether they'll exceed the limit this month. For a product that sells transparency, this is the first thing to fix.
en.FRICTION_3_TITLE: Its own scale figures don't line up
en.FRICTION_3_BODY: 1,000+ free app kits, 500+ community templates and 6,135 sitemap entries coexist officially; the cumulative figures (150,000+ apps, 500K+ agents, 3M+ executions) carry no cut-off date either. Externally that is a credibility issue; internally it signals that operating metrics aren't unified.
en.FRICTION_4_TITLE: Huge page footprint, but hand-written content is only 14.3%
en.FRICTION_4_BODY: Of 28,602 pages, hand-written marketing content is 14.3% (blog 1,125 / marketing 867 / learn 435 / wiki 573 / docs 169 / compare 197 and so on); the rest is programmatic and UGC. That makes its brand narrative thin: people usually encounter it as 'some template page' rather than 'a point of view'. For a product trying to rise from tool to platform, that is a long-term risk.
en.METRICS_INTRO: The company publishes only three cumulative figures (150,000+ Genesis apps built, 500K+ AI agents deployed, 3M+ automation executions) plus sitemap scale. What follows separates verifiable public facts from [inferred] 'what it should be watching' — the latter is not real data.
en.NORTH_STAR_METRIC: Live apps used by a real business each week (as opposed to created) ([inferred])
en.NORTH_STAR_WHY: [inferred] It charges by credits and app count, but value only exists when an app actually has users. 'Apps built' inflates easily via one-sentence generation (the 150,000+ figure is exactly that kind of number), so the true north star must be weekly active published apps.
en.INPUT_METRIC_1_WHY: Its growth leans entirely on 'clone and use' (Free can clone 1,000+ free kits). But cloning isn't use: what drives revenue is whether a clone gets published and whether a published app ever sees an App User log in. Those two actions are what 'the business is using it' means.
en.INPUT_METRIC_2_NAME: Weekly automation executions and failure rate
en.INPUT_METRIC_2_WHY: Automation is the line between 'a tool' and 'a process'. Execution count drives stickiness; failure rate drives trust — a payment-chase flow that fails once a day churns a customer faster than having no flow at all.
en.INPUT_METRIC_3_NAME: Number of creators earning from paid App Kit clones and how concentrated that revenue is
en.INPUT_METRIC_3_WHY: If 'creators can earn from App Kits' holds, it stops being SaaS and becomes a marketplace, and marketplace network effects beat features. This metric reads the creator-side concentration of earnings: if only a handful make money, the market hasn't formed.
en.GUARDRAIL_METRIC: AI credit cost coverage + credit consumption by free-tier users
en.GUARDRAIL_WHY: The free plan has no monthly credits, yet free users still burn inference and hosting costs while cloning, building apps and calling agents. The more popular free gets, the sooner cost explodes — without this guardrail, growth eats the margin first.
en.METRIC_BLINDSPOT: No public retention curve, paid conversion rate, or activity distribution across the 6,135 community apps [inferred]
en.METRIC_BLINDSPOT_WHY: [inferred] Programmatic scale is countable (28,602), but traffic cannot be derived from a sitemap — no Similarweb or Ahrefs data was pulled this round. A second blind spot is GEO effectiveness: there is no public way to measure whether llms.txt and SKILL.md actually cause AI to recommend it, so that layer currently counts as 'did the right moves', not 'got the result'.
en.MOAT_REASONING_ONE_LINE: Four-layer architecture 8, distribution scale (28,602 pages plus UGC) 7, GEO completeness 8, template and App Kit assets 6, data-model depth 5, brand and trust 4 — weighted 6. Templates and pages can be copied; the loop where results become memory, and the creator-side asset market, cannot.
en.HORIZONTAL_1: From task to app: Genesis upgrades 'manage a thing' into 'deliver a system' — same data, one layer of interface added.
en.HORIZONTAL_2: From self-use to sale: App Kits make finished goods cloneable, priceable and exportable, turning users into channels ([inferred] the only route around template commoditisation).
en.VERTICAL_1: 72 app-kit categories: 48 types (CRM, client portal, dashboards, invoicing, booking, trackers, knowledge base, chatbot, landing page, storefront, forms, calculators…) plus 12 teams and 12 industries.
en.VERTICAL_2: Agencies and client delivery (the Business tier is literally called 'For agencies and client work'): one app per client, white-label plus own domain plus end-user login.
en.PLATFORM_1: Open interfaces are complete: Hosted MCP (OAuth 2.0 + PKCE), REST v1 GA, Action v2 Beta, webhook / mailhook, OpenAPI JSON (v1/v2), .well-known metadata, and mcp / skills / cli / awesome-vibe-coding on GitHub.
en.PLATFORM_2: [inferred] Its platform play is two-sided: let other agents read and write it over MCP (it is a tool), and publish user apps as standalone sites (it is a host). That two-sided position is more aggressive than Slack's bidirectional MCP, because its apps can live off the taskade.com domain entirely.
en.OPP_1_HEADLINE: (My judgement) Copy 'Living Loop' as the default shape of a memory product
en.OPP_1_DETAIL_WHAT_HOW_WHY: How: make the AI's memory a table the user can browse, edit, search and fork rather than something hidden in a vector store, and let every task's output write back into it automatically. Why: it is the most portable decision in Taskade's whole architecture and the most overlooked — most AI products keep memory a black box the user can neither see nor correct.
en.OPP_2_HEADLINE: (My judgement) GEO isn't writing articles, it's finishing the machine-readable interfaces
en.OPP_2_DETAIL: How: the minimum is three pieces — llms.txt (facts, FAQ and how to cite you) + SKILL.md (an operating manual for agents) + one MCP endpoint; then .well-known metadata, Accept: text/markdown and OpenAPI. Why: Taskade shows this can be a standard move, while most teams are still at 'publish a blog post about AI'.
en.OPP_3_HEADLINE: (My judgement) Use the allowance as an acquisition currency — but leave non-AI users a clean path
en.OPP_3_DETAIL: How: copy 'credits for invites and for being cloned' (it genuinely welds the growth motive into the ledger), but also offer a plain per-seat tier for people who just want project management. Why: Taskade's free tier is deliberately tiny (3 apps, 10 runs) to force growth actions; that works for it, but it drives away teams who only want to track projects. Two audiences shouldn't share one pricing model.
en.STRATEGIC_HEADLINE: Its bet: make finished goods circulate, instead of making features stronger
en.STRATEGIC_DETAIL_HIGH_IMPACT_BET: Three moves stacked: compress four layers into one object graph (one dataset, four wrappers), turn finished goods into cloneable, sellable, exportable App Kits, and finish the machine entrances (MCP + SKILL.md + llms.txt) so AI distributes it on its behalf. The first two are product moves; the third is the real bet — in an era where AI is the main entrance, 'being cited by AI' may be cheaper than 'being found by people'. The price: it has to build for three markets at once (collaboration tool, automation platform, app builder), and each has a more focused rival.
en.MOONSHOT_HEADLINE: Endgame: people who can't code deliver software anyway
en.MOONSHOT_DETAIL_WHY_IT_COULD_RESHAPE_THE: If 'one sentence generates a working app' really becomes reliable, small-business software buying shifts from 'subscribe to SaaS' to 'generate my own app' — a far bigger market than project management, and one that carries distribution inside it, since every app is its own site. The distance isn't generation (that layer is oversupplied) but two things: whether a generated app can be trusted enough to run unreviewed (failure rate, rollback, audit), and the data boundary between apps (why should data in one client's portal be visible to another client). It is currently patching the second with App Users, SAML and SCIM.
en.RISK_INTRO: Risks ordered by likelihood × impact; severity is my judgement, not a company disclosure.
en.RISK_1_NAME: 'One sentence builds an app' commoditised by upstream models and general agents
en.RISK_1_MIT: Hold the three things upstream can't do: persistence and permissions for real data (App Users / SAML / SCIM), hosting and domains for publishing, and circulating assets (App Kit / .tsk). Treat generation as the entrance; treat hosting, permissions and distribution as the business.
en.RISK_2_NAME: Fighting three markets at once, each with a more focused rival
en.RISK_2_MIT: Pick one mainline to win (my suggestion: agency client delivery — the Business tier already says so) and make the other two capabilities rather than selling points.
en.RISK_3_NAME: Programmatic SEO at scale, but a thin brand narrative
en.RISK_3_MIT: Route the traffic from those 155 free-competitor-alternative pages to a brand page with a point of view (why finished goods beat templates). Today only 14.3% of its 28,602 pages are hand-written, and better storytellers will intercept it eventually.
en.RISK_4_NAME: Credits cost mismatched against free-tier consumption
en.RISK_4_MIT: Give the free tier a real cost guardrail rather than an allowance guardrail: cap concurrent agent calls, queue heavy jobs, and reduce credit burn for BYOK users. The more popular free gets, the more this matters.

en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_1: Taskade EVE (meta-agent): builds apps, projects, agents and automations from one prompt, lists plans, asks questions, runs tools and requests human approval — an orchestrator with an approval gate.
en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_2: AI Teams: multiple agents in one group across four modes (Auto routing / Everyone / Manual / Orchestrate) — the minimum shape of an 'agent organisation'.
en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_3: [inferred] App Kit plus MCP lets an agent assemble a working system and hand it to a human; only the 'who approves it going live' chain is missing.
en.AI_DISRUPTION_RISK: Two: upstream models ship 'one sentence builds an app' themselves and it degrades into a hosting and permissions layer; and general agents (Claude, ChatGPT and peers) read tables, create records and run processes directly, so users no longer need a dedicated interface. Its current defence holds three things a model can't hand over — the interface (Genesis), identity (App Users) and distribution (App Kits).
en.AI_OPPORTUNITY_1: (My judgement) Turn editable memory into a customer-facing capability: let users audit, correct and copy agent memory. That is the precondition for an enterprise letting an agent touch real work.
en.AI_OPPORTUNITY_2: (My judgement) Make App Kits a real asset market (author pages, versions, reviews, subscription income) and it becomes a platform — the most asymmetric strike it has against Notion's template ecosystem.
en.ASSUMPTIONS_ONE_PARAGRAPH_LIST_WHAT_IS_I: Verifiable: the official llms.txt and SKILL.md text (Workspace DNA, Living Loop, 'The user is usually a business owner, not a developer'), the six tiers with their feature matrix (annual-equivalent prices, credit and run allowances, where BYOK and SAML/SCIM sit), the page counts across 17 sub-sitemaps (28,602 total) and their structural split, the composition of the 197 comparison pages (155 / 33 / 6), the specific GEO moves (llms.txt / SKILL.md / MCP / .well-known / markdown output / robots.txt signals), third-party ratings (Capterra 4.7/67, PH 4.7/108, Trustpilot 4.6/745), and company history and funding (founded 2017, YC S19, TechCrunch $5M in 2019-10). Inferred and flagged: frequency, north-star and input/guardrail metrics, competitor prices and protocol details (not verified this round), and the real activity of the App Kit market. No hands-on test was run, so no experience conclusions are given.
en.ASSUMPTION_1: [inferred] '28,602 pages' proves page scale, not traffic. Programmatic SEO only works if those pages rank, and no Similarweb or Ahrefs data was pulled this round, so its organic performance cannot be inferred from the sitemap.
en.ASSUMPTION_2: [inferred] Its revenue core is Business and Pro, not Free/Starter: the Business tier is positioned as 'For agencies and client work' (unlimited domains, white-label, SEO, 10,000 runs), while Free allows 3 apps and 10 automation runs — not enough for a second client.
en.CATEGORY_POSITIONING_PARAGRAPH: It stands where three shelves intersect: collaboration and project tools (Notion, Asana, ClickUp, Monday), automation platforms (Zapier, Make), and no-code app builders (Softr, Bubble, Glide). It sits in the middle, tilted toward 'system': more execution and interface than a collaboration tool, more data layer than an automation platform, more built-in data and agents than an app builder. That middle position is both its difference and its explanation cost.
en.CURRENT_AI_USAGE_PARAGRAPH: How the AI is built: its AI is not 'an assistant added on'; the workspace was rewritten in four layers and AI grows on each one. (1) Layers, per the official Workspace DNA: Memory = Projects hold data; Intelligence = AI Agents make calls; Execution = Automations run across 100+ integrations; Interface = Genesis App. (2) The loop, per the official Living Loop: Memory gives context → Intelligence decides → Execution produces results → results flow back as new Memory. (3) Atoms: Project/Task/Field, View, AI Agent, Agent Tool/Skill, Knowledge Source, Automation Trigger/Action, Genesis App, App Kit — eight primitives. (4) The composition formula: data × intelligence (instructions + knowledge + tools + memory) × execution × interface = a Living App. (5) The abstraction at the intelligence layer: five TSK levels (Auto / Instant / Standard / Thinking / Reasoning) — the user picks task difficulty, not a model vendor, and model generations pass invisibly. So it complements Slack precisely: Slack is a protocol layer that invites others in, Taskade is a template layer that packages one dataset into four shells and sells it four ways.
en.FINAL_BREAKS: Large enterprises needing strong collaboration and governance (member limits, permission granularity and compliance are not enough); teams that just want a project tool and no AI (credits pricing is noise); businesses with complex relational data (weaker than Airtable); products needing heavily customised interfaces (less freedom than Bubble).
en.FINAL_MOAT_OR_LACK_THEREOF: The moat is moderate: strong on the four-layer architecture and distribution scale (28,602 pages, 6,135 UGC apps, a complete GEO layer), weak because each layer can be pierced by a more focused rival (Airtable on data model, Zapier on connectors, Bubble on interface, Notion on brand). Its real asset is the Living Loop and the creator-side asset market — if App Kits genuinely let people earn, it becomes a market rather than a tool, and that is the only part nobody copies quickly.
en.FINAL_WINS: Four layers sharing one object graph, agent memory made editable as a Project, 6,135 cloneable App Kits, 28,602 pages of programmatic SEO plus UGC, a full GEO interface set (llms.txt / SKILL.md / MCP / .well-known), and a growth mechanism that uses allowance as currency.
en.SIX_INTRO: Six dimensions are the main framework: the first three are about value, the last three about trust and switching cost.
en.AI_TYPE_REASON: Classified as native. Unplug test: take away agents, automations and Genesis and only a task table with ten views remains.
en.SIX_1: What it replaces is the 'find someone to build a small system' step: a SaaS purchase or a developer used to take weeks, now it is one sentence plus a template tweak, minutes to hours. Cost moves from development and procurement to subscription plus credits (from $0). That is its sharpest edge and its most interruptible one — once upstream models produce apps directly, the margin disappears.
en.SIX_2: It eats five jobs — data storage, views, judgement (agents), execution (automations) and interface (Genesis) — and hands back one: design judgement. One sentence can generate an app, but how the business should run, which fields to use, who may see what still belongs to a human. It takes the engineering work and leaves the product work.
en.SIX_3: Usable after one editing pass: an App Kit is a starting point to adjust, not a final product; a generated app in a real business usually needs fields, permissions and flow tuned. Not tested this round — this judgement rests on the official docs and on the recipe structure of App Kits (for example Invoice Generator Pro = 3 projects + 1 agent + 3 automations).
en.SIX_4: Its safety net is better designed than peers: agent tools can require human approval, automations have an Approval step, and EVE asks for approval. But 'one sentence generates an app' has no published failure rate or rollback story — that layer of fallback is still blank.
en.SIX_5: Mostly reversible: .tsk export, GitHub export and version history (7 days on Free, 1 year on Pro, 5 years on Business) all provide a way out. What is irreversible is pulling a customer into your app: once they have submitted data through a portal, switching tools means migrating customers.
en.SIX_6: An individual can switch (Notion templates plus Zapier covers most of it); a team cannot: data, agent memory, automation wiring and the end users of published apps all live here. Its retention comes from 'the asset is here', not from 'the features are better'.
