extra_zh.title: 对标竞品地图
extra_zh.body:
这份名单不靠猜，直接读它自己的对比页结构：197 条 /compare/* 里，155 条是 free-<竞品>-alternative（free-notion-alternative、free-zapier-alternative 这类），33 条是纯第三方模型对比（gpt-vs-claude、qwen-vs-kimi、glm-vs-gpt，与产品无关），只有 6 条是 taskade-vs-*。也就是说它的 SEO 主战场不是「品牌对比」，是「免费替代品」这个搜索意图——谁被搜成「XX 的免费替代」，谁就是它的对手。

谁抢同一个需求抢同一段链路用户实际迁移
Notion同一个需求：想要一个「什么都能放」的工作区的小团队与创作者数据与文档这一段（Notion 是 block 模型，Taskade 是 project/task/field 模型）它给 Notion 备了 free-notion-alternative 页，另一头又有 30+ 导入器直接从 Notion 搬数据——两头都在打
Asana / ClickUp / Monday / Trello要「项目被跟踪」的团队任务与流程这一段（Taskade 用 project + automation 接）对应 4 个 free-alternative 页 + 导入器；但它真正的差异不是项目管理，是「项目能变成 app」
Zapier / Make已经有工具、只需要把工具连起来的人自动化这一段（触发-动作编排）它的 automate（2,361 页）+ integrations（180 页）正对着打；但 Zapier 不持有数据层，这是它的机会
Softr / Bubble / Glide要「把数据做成一个能给客户用的界面」的人界面这一段——这是 Genesis 最直接的对手这一格它最难赢：对方的界面自由度更高，而它靠「数据+agent+自动化一体」来换
Airtable要强结构化数据与视图的团队数据模型这一段复杂业务会被 Airtable 挡住；Taskade 用「流程 + agent」而不是「字段能力」来避战
通用 AI agent（ChatGPT / Claude 等）所有想「说一句话就把活干了」的人智能这一段，且不持界面的包袱最不确定的一路：如果用户直接跟 agent 说话，中间那层工作区就多余了

读法：它在地图上的位置很独特——不在「项目管理」的正中央，而在「协作工具 × 自动化 × app builder」的三角中段。好处是几乎没有同构的对手；坏处是每一格都有一个更专注的强者，用户随时可以说「我为什么不直接用 Zapier + Bubble」。竞品价格本次全部未核验，不做价格对比。

extra_zh.title: 竞品技术底座
extra_zh.body:
AI 构建过程（Taskade 怎么把原子拼成工作流）：① 四层——Memory（Projects 存数据）/ Intelligence（Agents 做判断）/ Execution（Automations 跨 100+ 集成执行）/ Interface（Genesis App 当界面）；② 一条环——Living Loop：Memory 给上下文 → Intelligence 做决定 → Execution 出结果 → 结果回流成新的 Memory；③ 八个基元——Project/Task/Field、View、AI Agent、Agent Tool/Skill、Knowledge Source、Automation Trigger/Action、Genesis App、App Kit；④ 一条公式——数据 × 智能（指令 + 知识 + 工具 + 记忆）× 执行 × 界面 = 一个 Living App。所以它的 AI 不是「加了一个助手」，而是把工作区按四层重写、再让 AI 长在每一层上。下表先摊开它自己的装配线，再看各家的底座锁住了什么。

产品底座它锁住了什么能力
Taskade一份对象图（Project/Task/Field）+ 四层封装（Projects / Agents / Automations / Genesis App）+ 模型路由（TSK 阶梯，可 BYOK）+ 托管与发布（自有域名、App Users）锁住「从数据到可交付界面」这一整条：别人卖其中一段，它把四段焊在一起
Notionblock 模型（页面即数据）+ 数据库视图 + 模板生态锁住「知识 + 文档」的心智与模板分发；自动化与执行是外挂
Airtable关系型 base + view + automation锁住「结构化数据建模」这一段：字段类型与关联能力是它的护城河
Zapier / Make触发-动作编排引擎 + 海量连接器锁住「系统之间的胶水」：连接器数量本身就是壁垒，但它不存数据、不做界面
Softr / Bubble / Glideno-code 界面构建器 + 外部数据源锁住「界面自由度」：能把界面做到像定制软件，但数据与 AI 要外接

[推断] 真护城河不在「一句话生成」，在「生成之后的那三件事」：数据存在哪、权限怎么给、产物怎么分发。因为生成能力是模型给的，任何人都能调；而 App Users（终端用户体系）、自有域名与 SSL、App Kit 的可克隆/可售卖/可导出，是产品自己搭的工程。Taskade 把这三件放在付费墙上（Business 起白标与 SEO、Enterprise 起 SCIM），说明它也知道钱在哪。
它最脆的一层是「生成」本身：一旦上游模型自己做到「一句话建 app 并托管」，它的入口价值就被抽走。所以它急着做 MCP + SKILL.md + llms.txt——不是因为时髦，是因为要确保即使 AI 变成入口，自己仍是那个被调用的执行层。

extra_zh.title: 可迁移的机会（我的判断）
extra_zh.body:
1. 把 「Living Loop」抄成记忆产品的默认结构——记忆落成用户可浏览、可编辑、可搜索、可 fork 的一张表，每次产出自动写回。为什么值得抄：这是它全套架构里最可迁移、也最容易被忽略的一招；大多数 AI 产品的记忆是黑盒，用户既看不见也改不了。最轻，改的是存储形态不是模型。
  2. GEO 不是写文章，是把机器可读接口做全——最低配三件套：llms.txt（事实 + FAQ + 该怎么引用我）、SKILL.md（给 agent 的操作手册）、一个 MCP 入口；进阶再加 .well-known、Accept: text/markdown、OpenAPI。为什么：它证明这套能做成标准动作，而多数团队还停在「写一篇讲 AI 的博客」。最快见效，一周能上。
  3. 把「额度」当拉新货币——邀请与被克隆给 credits，是新用户拿到额度的唯一路径，等于把增长动机焊进账本。但要给「我只想用基础功能」的用户一条干净的路（纯席位价），别让两种用户共用一套计价。
  4. 让用户的产出自动带发现层——每个已发布作品自动产出 robots/sitemap/llms.txt。做任何「用户作品」类产品，这一层应该默认打开：UGC 直接变成搜索与 AI 发现节点。最难被抄，因为它要求你的产品先有「已发布的作品」。

四个里哪个最该先做？第 2 个：它不依赖产品改造，只依赖把「给机器看的那一页」写对。哪个最容易被忽略？第 1 个——大家都把记忆当技术问题，其实它是产品问题：用户能不能看见、能不能改。

extra_zh.title: 流量与变现拆解
extra_zh.body:
先把规模摊开（官方 sitemap 实测，2026-11-26，17 个子 sitemap 合计 28,602 条 URL）。结构比总量更重要：程序化资源页 18,376 页 = 64.2%（templates 3,997 / generate 4,526 / agents 3,169 / automate 2,361 / prompts 2,205 / convert 2,118）、UGC app 页 6,135 页 = 21.4%（community apps + 495 个作者页）、手写营销内容只占 14.3%（blog 1,125 / marketing 867 / wiki 573 / learn 435 / docs 169 / compare 197 / integrations 180 / ai 43 等）。再叠一层别人没有的：GEO 发现层——llms.txt（含 How to Cite Taskade 的指定引用措辞）+ SKILL.md + Hosted MCP + .well-known 元数据 + Accept: text/markdown + OpenAPI + TSK-Bench，robots.txt 明确 ai-train=yes / search=yes / ai-input=yes。

环节它怎么做的为什么有效 / 哪里漏
拉新程序化资源页 18,376 条 + 197 条对比页（155 条 free-竞品-alternative）+ UGC 6,135 条 + GEO 层有效：搜索意图覆盖极全，「免费替代品」这种高转化词都有页接。漏点：sitemap 只证明页面规模，不证明流量；本期未取 Similarweb/Ahrefs
激活克隆即用（Free 可克隆 1,000+ free kits）+ 一句话建 app + 模板改一改有效：新人一上手就在用「别人的成品」，不是空工作区。漏点：克隆占 Free 的 3 个 app 额度，第二次克隆就撞墙
留存数据 + agent 记忆 + 自动化接线 + 已发布 app 的终端用户（App Users）有效：四层都在它这里，迁走等于重建业务。漏点：留存的前提是「真的跑起来了」，而 6,135 个社区 app 的活跃分布未核验
变现订阅 + credits：Free $0 / Starter $6 / Pro $10（月付 $20）/ Business $25 / Max $100 / Enterprise $250有效：付费墙立在「开始对外交付」那一刻（更多成员、更多 app、自有域名、白标）。漏点：credits 与 runs 两种货币，预算算不清
扩张成员数 × app 数 × credits 三轴同时扩张；Business 起无限成员与域名；Enterprise 加 SCIM[推断] 扩张最顺的一轴是「代理机构」：一个客户一个 app，天然推动 app 数与域名数同时上涨

套利三问。钱从谁的兜里出：小企业主与代理机构的经营预算（不是 IT 预算），所以它用信用卡可付的 $6–$25 档做主力，而不是先攻企业。还能拿多久：[推断] 「程序化 SEO + UGC + GEO」这三层的组合窗口还有 1–2 年；一旦所有人都做 llms.txt，这一层的相对优势会归零。凭什么你拿到：凭它把「生成 → 托管 → 权限 → 分发」四段焊在一起，而这四段的工程难度递增——生成最容易，托管与权限最难。

最脆的那根梁：「一句话生成」这个入口。它既是它最响的卖点，也是最容易被上游吃掉的一层。真正的护城河在入口之后——已发布 app 的终端用户、可售卖的 App Kit、以及每个 app 自带的发现层。如果它继续把营销重心放在「一句话」，就会一直站在最容易被替代的位置上；如果重心移到「成品资产」，它才站得住。

extra_en.title: Competitive map
extra_en.body:
This list isn't guesswork; read its own comparison pages. Of 197 /compare/* URLs, 155 are free-<competitor>-alternative (free-notion-alternative, free-zapier-alternative and similar), 33 are pure third-party model comparisons (gpt-vs-claude, qwen-vs-kimi, glm-vs-gpt — unrelated to the product), and only 6 are taskade-vs-*. Its SEO battleground isn't brand comparison but the 'free alternative' intent — whoever gets searched as 'a free alternative to X' is a rival.

WhoFighting for the same needFighting for the same link in the chainWhere users actually go
NotionThe same need: one workspace where everything fits, for small teams and creatorsData and documents (Notion's block model versus Taskade's project/task/field model)It keeps a free-notion-alternative page for Notion, and 30+ importers pulling data out of Notion — attacking from both sides
Asana / ClickUp / Monday / TrelloTeams that need projects trackedThe task-and-process link (Taskade answers with projects plus automations)Four free-alternative pages plus importers; but its real difference isn't project management, it's that a project can become an app
Zapier / MakePeople who already have tools and only need them connectedThe automation link (trigger-action orchestration)Its automate (2,361 pages) and integrations (180 pages) point straight at it; Zapier holds no data layer, which is the opening
Softr / Bubble / GlidePeople who want data turned into an interface a client can useThe interface link — Genesis's most direct rivalsThe hardest cell to win: their interface freedom is higher, and Taskade trades on data + agents + automation being in one place
AirtableTeams needing strong structured data and viewsThe data-model linkComplex businesses get blocked by Airtable; Taskade avoids the fight by selling process and agents rather than field power
General AI agents (ChatGPT / Claude and peers)Everyone who wants to 'say one sentence and have it done'The intelligence link, with no interface baggageThe least certain front: if users talk to an agent directly, the workspace in between becomes optional

How to read the map: its position is unusual — not the centre of project management but the middle of the collaboration × automation × app-builder triangle. The upside is that almost nobody is isomorphic to it; the downside is that every cell has a more focused specialist, and a user can always ask 'why not just Zapier plus Bubble?'. Competitor prices were not verified this round, so no price comparison is offered.

extra_en.title: Rivals' technical base
extra_en.body:
How the AI is built (turning atoms into workflows): (1) four layers — Memory (Projects hold data) / Intelligence (Agents decide) / Execution (Automations across 100+ integrations) / Interface (Genesis App); (2) one loop — the Living Loop: Memory gives context → Intelligence decides → Execution produces results → results flow back as new Memory; (3) eight primitives — Project/Task/Field, View, AI Agent, Agent Tool/Skill, Knowledge Source, Automation Trigger/Action, Genesis App, App Kit; (4) one formula — data × intelligence (instructions + knowledge + tools + memory) × execution × interface = a Living App. So its AI is not 'an assistant added on' but a workspace rewritten in four layers with AI growing on each one. The table below opens its own assembly line first, then what each rival's base locks up.

ProductBaseWhat that base locks up
TaskadeOne object graph (Project/Task/Field) + four wrappers (Projects / Agents / Automations / Genesis App) + model routing (the TSK ladder, BYOK allowed) + hosting and publishing (own domain, App Users)Locks up the whole path from data to a deliverable interface: rivals sell a segment, it welds the four together
NotionThe block model (a page is data) plus database views and a template ecosystemLocks up the 'knowledge and documents' mindshare and template distribution; automation and execution are bolt-ons
AirtableRelational bases plus views and automationLocks up structured data modelling: field types and relations are its moat
Zapier / MakeA trigger-action engine plus a very large connector libraryLocks up the glue between systems — connector count is itself a barrier — but it stores no data and builds no interface
Softr / Bubble / GlideNo-code interface builders on top of external data sourcesLocks up interface freedom: they can look like custom software, but data and AI come from outside

[inferred] The real moat isn't 'one sentence generates' — it's the three things after generation: where the data lives, how permissions are handed out, and how the output is distributed. Generation comes from a model anyone can call; App Users (an end-user system), own domains with SSL, and cloneable/sellable/exportable App Kits are engineering Taskade built itself. It puts those on the paywall (white-label and SEO from Business, SCIM on Enterprise), which shows it knows where the money is.
Its most fragile layer is generation itself: once an upstream model can build and host an app from one sentence, its entry value is siphoned off. That is why it rushed MCP + SKILL.md + llms.txt — not for fashion, but to make sure that even if AI becomes the entrance, it remains the execution layer being called.

extra_en.title: Portable opportunities (my judgement)
extra_en.body:
1. Copy the Living Loop as the default shape of a memory product — memory lands as a table the user can browse, edit, search and fork, and every output writes back automatically. Why: it is the most portable and most overlooked decision in its architecture; most AI products keep memory a black box the user can neither see nor correct. Lightest option — it changes storage shape, not the model.
  2. GEO isn't writing articles, it's finishing the machine-readable interfaces — minimum: llms.txt (facts + FAQ + how to cite you), SKILL.md (an agent operating manual), one MCP endpoint; then .well-known, Accept: text/markdown, OpenAPI. Why: it proves this can be a standard move while most teams are still writing blog posts about AI. Fastest payoff — a week's work.
  3. Use the allowance as an acquisition currency — credits for invites and for being cloned is the only route to allowance, which welds the growth motive into the ledger. But leave a clean path (a plain per-seat price) for people who only want the basic product; two audiences shouldn't share one pricing model.
  4. Ship a discovery layer with every user output — every published artifact automatically produces robots/sitemap/llms.txt. For any product with 'user work', this should be on by default: UGC becomes a search and AI discovery node. Hardest to copy, because it requires your product to have published artifacts first.

Which first? Number 2 — it needs no product rebuild, only that you write the machine-facing page properly. Which gets ignored? Number 1 — everyone treats memory as a technical problem when it is a product problem: can the user see it, and can they change it?

extra_en.title: Traffic and monetisation
extra_en.body:
First the scale (official sitemaps measured 2026-11-26; 17 sub-sitemaps totalling 28,602 URLs). The structure matters more than the total: programmatic resource pages 18,376 = 64.2% (templates 3,997 / generate 4,526 / agents 3,169 / automate 2,361 / prompts 2,205 / convert 2,118), UGC app pages 6,135 = 21.4% (community apps plus 495 author pages), and hand-written marketing content only 14.3% (blog 1,125 / marketing 867 / wiki 573 / learn 435 / docs 169 / compare 197 / integrations 180 / ai 43 and so on). Then a layer nobody else has: the GEO discovery layer — llms.txt (including a 'How to Cite Taskade' instruction), SKILL.md, Hosted MCP, .well-known metadata, Accept: text/markdown, OpenAPI and TSK-Bench, with robots.txt stating ai-train=yes / search=yes / ai-input=yes.

StageWhat it doesWhy it works / where it leaks
Acquisition18,376 programmatic resource pages + 197 comparison pages (155 free-competitor-alternative) + 6,135 UGC pages + the GEO layerWorks: search intent coverage is very broad, including high-converting 'free alternative' terms. Leak: a sitemap proves page scale, not traffic; no Similarweb/Ahrefs data this round
ActivationClone and use (Free can clone 1,000+ free kits) + one-sentence Genesis + adjust a templateWorks: a newcomer starts from someone else's finished app, not an empty workspace. Leak: a clone consumes one of Free's 3 app slots, so the second clone hits the wall
RetentionData + agent memory + automation wiring + the end users of published apps (App Users)Works: all four live here, so leaving means rebuilding the business. Leak: retention presumes the app actually runs, and the activity distribution of those 6,135 community apps was not verified
MonetisationSubscription plus credits: Free $0 / Starter $6 / Pro $10 (monthly $20) / Business $25 / Max $100 / Enterprise $250Works: the paywall stands at the moment you start delivering outward (more members, more apps, own domain, white-label). Leak: credits and runs are two currencies, so budgets can't be forecast
ExpansionThree axes at once — members, apps and credits; unlimited members and domains from Business; SCIM on Enterprise[inferred] The smoothest axis is agencies: one app per client naturally pushes both app count and domain count up

The three arbitrage questions. Whose pocket does the money come from: the operating budget of small businesses and agencies (not IT budget), which is why the $6–$25 credit-card tiers are the main line rather than enterprise-first. How long can it keep taking it: [inferred] the combination of programmatic SEO + UGC + GEO has a one-to-two-year window; once everyone ships llms.txt, the relative advantage goes to zero. Why does it get it: because it welds generation → hosting → permissions → distribution together, and the engineering difficulty rises along that chain — generation is easiest, hosting and permissions are hardest.

The weakest beam: the 'one sentence generates' entrance. It is both its loudest selling point and the layer most easily eaten upstream. The real moat sits after the entrance — the end users of published apps, sellable App Kits, and the discovery layer each app carries. As long as marketing stays on 'one sentence', it stands where it is easiest to replace; when the emphasis moves to 'finished assets', it stands up.
